title: Conic polarity as a typed point-to-line map
revised_question: Which nonsingular conic defines the point-line correspondence, and what is its dual conic?
status: Classical result developed and example checked
summary: The corrected construction identifies the quadratic form first, then derives polarity, the dual conic and coordinate covariance. It removes the undefined polar-line formula and the invented idea that one point dualizes to a conic.
definitions_json: ["Let Q be an invertible symmetric 3×3 matrix over a field of characteristic different from two. Points are nonzero column vectors modulo scale; lines are nonzero covectors modulo scale.","The nonsingular conic is C={x:xᵀQx=0}. The polar line of p has covector ℓ=Qp, because its equation is pᵀQx=0."]
theorem_name: Polarity and the dual quadratic form
theorem_statement: The polarity p↦Qp is invertible, incidence is reciprocal, and the tangent-line locus in the dual projective plane is ℓᵀQ⁻¹ℓ=0.
theorem_proof: At a conic point a, differentiating xᵀQx gives tangent covector 2Qa, which defines the same projective line as Qa. Conversely any ℓ has pole p=Q⁻¹ℓ. That line is tangent precisely when its pole lies on C, which is exactly ℓᵀQ⁻¹ℓ=0. Reciprocity follows from pᵀQq=qᵀQp. Under x′=Mx, Q′=M⁻ᵀQM⁻¹ and ℓ′=M⁻ᵀℓ; hence Q′p′=M⁻ᵀQp. The construction therefore respects projective coordinate changes rather than depending on one affine drawing.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Use the real unit-circle conic x²+y²−z²=0 and p=(2,0,1).","calculation":"Here Q=diag(1,1,−1), so the polar is 2x−z=0. Its intersections with the conic are a±=(1/2,±√3/2,1). The tangents at these points have covectors (1/2,±√3/2,−1), and each contains p because their pairing with p is zero. The polar itself is not tangent: its dual quadratic value is 2²−1²=3.","conclusion":"The polar joins the two contact points of tangents drawn from the exterior point. Applying Q⁻¹ to its covector returns p. This verifies the point-line correspondence and the dual-conic test separately."}
limits: Invertibility of Q and the characteristic assumption matter. A degenerate quadratic form does not produce a global polarity. Real exterior/interior terminology has no direct analogue over every field; projective incidence survives, while real tangent counts may change.
extension: For higher-dimensional quadrics the same matrix argument defines polar hyperplanes. A useful further problem is to classify how the construction degenerates as det Q tends to zero and which incidence statements remain valid.

title: Cross-ratio with a fixed ordering and homogeneous coordinates
revised_question: Which ordered four points are harmonic, and what precisely is preserved by a projective transformation?
status: Classical result developed and example checked
summary: Cross-ratio becomes a precise projective invariant once the four-point order and convention are fixed. Harmonicity is then a concrete value of that invariant, not an order-free label.
definitions_json: ["For distinct projective points a,b,c,d on P¹, choose nonzero representatives v_a,…,v_d and write [u,v]=det(u,v).","Use CR(a,b;c,d)=[v_a,v_c][v_b,v_d]/([v_b,v_c][v_a,v_d]). In an affine chart this is ((c−a)(d−b))/((c−b)(d−a))."]
theorem_name: Projective invariance and harmonic ordering
theorem_statement: Every invertible 2×2 matrix preserves this ordered cross-ratio. Under permutations the possible values lie in {r,1/r,1−r,1/(1−r),r/(r−1),(r−1)/r}.
theorem_proof: Rescaling any representative multiplies one numerator factor and one denominator factor by the same scalar. Applying M multiplies each bracket by det M; the two determinant factors above and below cancel. Thus CR is both projectively well defined and invariant. The permutation formulas follow by swapping arguments in the affine expression. In particular r=−1 can become 2 or 1/2 after a different ordering, so a harmonic assertion must retain its convention. Homogeneous representatives make the point at infinity routine rather than an exception requiring an invented formula.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take (a,b;c,d)=(−1,1;0,∞) and T(z)=(2z+3)/(z+2).","calculation":"Using v∞=(1,0) gives CR=−1. The transformation has nonzero determinant one and sends the ordered tuple to (1,5/3;3/2,2). The transformed ratio is [(1/2)(1/3)]/[(-1/6)(1)]=−1, verified with rational arithmetic.","conclusion":"The example simultaneously checks infinity, ordering and projective invariance. A dual statement for four concurrent lines follows only after identifying their pencil with P¹; duality is not a license to replace undefined point coordinates by arbitrary line expressions."}
limits: The four points must be distinct for the displayed nondegenerate ratio. Coinciding points require a limiting or compactified configuration-space interpretation. Over a general field, the listed six values can coincide more than they do over the real numbers.
extension: Cross-ratio coordinates give a concrete entry into moduli of marked projective lines: normalize three points to 0,1,∞ and the fourth is the remaining parameter. Investigate degenerations by tracking this parameter toward 0,1 or ∞.

title: A Heisenberg field and its verified local algebra
revised_question: Which algebra of fields is intended, and how does its formal local expression relate to a geometric formulation?
status: Classical result developed and example checked
summary: A worked Fock-space model supplies actual operators, a vacuum and a singular operator product. It shows what the abstract vertex-algebra vocabulary is organizing, without claiming that a few words or one OPE alone constitute the full theory.
definitions_json: ["Let F=C[x₁,x₂,…], with each polynomial involving finitely many variables. Set a₋ₙ=xₙ by multiplication and aₙ=n∂/∂xₙ for n>0; let a₀ act as zero.","The vacuum is 1. The current is J(z)=Σ_(n∈Z)aₙz^(−n−1), interpreted as a formal field. Normal ordering moves creation modes a₋ₙ to the left."]
theorem_name: Fock commutator and current contraction
theorem_statement: [a_m,a_n]=mδ_(m+n,0)I. The singular contraction of J(z)J(w) is 1/(z−w)², in the formal expansion associated with |z|>|w|.
theorem_proof: For positive m,n, derivatives commute and multiplications commute. The only nonzero mixed commutator is [m∂ₓₘ,xₙ]=mδ_mn. Splitting the field into annihilation and creation parts gives [J₊(z),J₋(w)]=Σ_(n≥1)n z^(−n−1)w^(n−1). Differentiating the formal geometric series Σ_(n≥0)wⁿz^(−n−1)=1/(z−w) produces the claimed double pole. The normally ordered remainder has no additional singular contraction. This calculation is a complete local commutator derivation in a defined representation.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Use the normally ordered stress tensor T(z)=(1/2):J(z)²: and vacuum states of low degree.","calculation":"The mode L₋₂ sends 1 to x₁²/2. The only contribution of L₂ on this state is (1/2)a₁², giving L₂L₋₂1=1/2. With L₀1=0, the Virasoro convention [L₂,L₋₂]=4L₀+cI/2 yields c=1. Translation on generators is represented by T₀=Σ_(n≥1)n xₙ₊₁∂ₓₙ, so [T₀,a₋ₙ]=n a₋₍ₙ₊₁₎.","conclusion":"The example fixes normalization of the central term and makes the relation between formal fields and modes explicit. The verifier checks the displayed operator relations on a finite set of polynomial states."}
limits: The finite checks do not prove all vertex-algebra axioms. The complete Heisenberg vertex algebra follows from the usual reconstruction construction, with vacuum, translation and locality stated on the full formal space. A coordinate-free chiral-algebra construction additionally needs a curve and coordinate transformation laws.
extension: Develop conformal blocks for this explicit algebra on a chosen curve, or prove a stated reconstruction theorem. Such a continuation has concrete input data rather than a generic appeal to string theory.

title: Four-site XXX spectrum and the regular one-magnon roots
revised_question: Which periodic spin chain and normalization produce the equations, and which eigenstates do the regular roots describe?
status: Classical result developed and example checked
summary: The corrected Bethe equations are tied to one Hamiltonian normalization and checked against a finite matrix. The resulting calculation verifies a sector, while keeping singular-root and completeness questions explicit.
definitions_json: ["Take N=4 periodic spin-1/2 sites and H=Σ_(j=0)^3(I−P_(j,j+1)), where P swaps adjacent spins and the last edge wraps around.","In the one-down-spin sector, |j⟩ denotes the down spin at site j. A plane wave has coefficients exp(ipj), with p=2πm/4."]
theorem_name: Exact one-magnon diagonalization
theorem_statement: H|p⟩=(2−2cos p)|p⟩, so this four-dimensional sector has energies 0,2,4,2. The finite regular Bethe roots are λ=1/2,0,−1/2, giving energies 1/(λ²+1/4)=2,4,2.
theorem_proof: Only the two bonds incident on the down spin act nontrivially, giving H|j⟩=2|j⟩−|j−1⟩−|j+1⟩. Substitution of the plane wave yields the dispersion. In the periodic XXX convention the regular roots obey ((λ_j+i/2)/(λ_j−i/2))^N=∏_(k≠j)(λ_j−λ_k+i)/(λ_j−λ_k−i). For one root the right side is one. Writing exp(ip)=(λ+i/2)/(λ−i/2) gives λ=(1/2)cot(p/2), and the energy agrees with the plane-wave dispersion. The p=0 state corresponds to the infinite-root limit.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Use real vectors in the ordered basis |0⟩,…,|3⟩.","calculation":"The vectors (1,1,1,1), (1,0,−1,0), (0,1,0,−1) and (1,−1,1,−1) form a basis with eigenvalues 0,2,2,4. Exact integer matrix multiplication verifies all four. For λ=1/2,0,−1/2 the complex Bethe ratio is i,−1,−i respectively; its fourth power is one.","conclusion":"This establishes agreement between a direct operator calculation and the regular Bethe description of the nonuniform one-magnon states. It also demonstrates why omitting the infinite-root state would lose an actual eigenvector."}
limits: The calculation does not prove completeness in other magnetization sectors or for arbitrary N. Roots at ±i/2 and coincident roots need a regularization or a carefully specified admissibility convention. Including the self-index k=j would add a spurious factor and changes the equations.

title: A complete two-site Gaudin to scalar-oper calculation
revised_question: Which established spectral correspondence is intended: Gaudin eigenvalues and opers, a q-oper correspondence, or another precisely stated construction?
status: Classical result developed and example checked
summary: A concrete spectral bridge replaces the unsupported Fourier-to-automorphic-form slogan. In the smallest nontrivial sl₂ example, the Bethe vector, Hamiltonian eigenvalues, Miura potential and cancellation of the apparent singularity can all be computed exactly. A rational three-site continuation also gives a complete eight-dimensional joint eigenbasis and two additional scalar-oper certificates.
definitions_json: ["On each C² take h=diag(1,−1), e|↓⟩=|↑⟩, f|↑⟩=|↓⟩ and Ω=(1/2)h⊗h+e⊗f+f⊗e. Choose marked points z₁=0,z₂=1.","Let H₁=Ω/(z₁−z₂)=−Ω and H₂=Ω. For weights (1,1), one Bethe root obeys 1/w+1/(w−1)=0."]
theorem_name: Singlet spectral data and apparent-pole cancellation
theorem_statement: The root w=1/2 yields a singlet with (H₁,H₂) eigenvalues (3/2,−3/2). Define u(x)=1/(2x)+1/(2(x−1))−1/(x−1/2). Then (∂−u)(∂+u)=∂²−V, where V=u²−u′=3/[4x²(x−1)²].
theorem_proof: The Bethe vector is w⁻¹|↓↑⟩+(w−1)⁻¹|↑↓⟩=2|↓↑⟩−2|↑↓⟩. Direct use of Ω gives eigenvalue −3/2, hence the Hamiltonian pair above. Near a root w, write u=−1/(x−w)+a₀+O(x−w). The double pole cancels in u²−u′, and its simple residue is −2a₀. Here a₀=(1/2)(1/w+1/(w−1))=0 precisely by the Bethe equation. Expanding at the physical points gives V=3/(4x²)+3/(4(x−1)²)+(3/2)/x−(3/2)/(x−1). Its simple residues match H₁ and H₂ in the declared normalization.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Treat the scalar differential equation y″−V(x)y=0 on the punctured projective line.","calculation":"The apparent point x=1/2 is absent from V. One solution is y₁=(x−1/2)/sqrt(x(x−1)). Reduction of order gives y₂=(x²−x/2+1/4)/sqrt(x(x−1)), with Wronskian one. Both are regular at x=1/2. Around x=0 or x=1 their common square-root factor changes sign, so monodromy is scalar and projectively trivial. The vacuum sector, with no root, instead has simple residues (−1/2,1/2), matching the triplet eigenvalues. For sites (0,1,8/3), the one-root equation reduces to 3w²−(22/3)w+8/3=0, with roots 2 and 4/9. Their eigenvalue triples are (−3/16,6/5,−81/80) and (25/16,−8/5,3/80). The highest vectors have one-down-spin coefficients (1/2,1,−3/2) and (9/4,−9/5,−9/20). Applying total lowering once to each gives two doublets; applying it zero through three times to the vacuum gives a quartet with eigenvalues (−11/16,1/5,39/80). All eight rational vectors are independent and satisfy all three full 8×8 Hamiltonians. For each regular root, with g=∏(x−z_i), u=g′/(2g)−1/(x−w) gives V=(3/4)Σ_i(x−z_i)^(−2)+Σ_iE_i/(x−z_i). Exact residual polynomials vanish. Since g′(w)=0, reduction of order has no logarithm: y₁=(x−w)/sqrt(g), y₂=[−g(w)+(g″(w)/2)(x−w)²+(x−w)³/2]/sqrt(g). Their Wronskian is one, and both ODE residuals vanish identically.","conclusion":"The calculation supplies an actual rank-one instance of the Gaudin–oper relationship: eigenvalues are encoded in coefficients of a scalar differential operator. The simple finite example is classical; its explicit replay is an exposition and verification result. The three-site continuation settles this complete finite joint-spectrum example, including its scalar equations, rather than leaving it as a proposed computation."}

title: Joint reliability is a dependence problem

status: Classical result developed and example checked
summary: The arithmetic correction is only the first step. An all-success probability cannot be identified from marginal accuracies alone. Exact dependence constructions show the full gap between what the individual probabilities say and what independence adds.
definitions_json: ["Let A₁,…,A_n be success events with P(A_i)=p_i. The target is P(∩A_i), a joint probability.","Mutual independence means P(∩_(i∈S)A_i)=∏_(i∈S)p_i for every subset S. Pairwise independence checks only subsets of size two."]
theorem_name: Fréchet bounds and an independence counterexample
theorem_statement: max(0,Σp_i−(n−1))≤P(∩A_i)≤min_i p_i. If all 104 marginals are 0.95, these bounds are 0 and 0.95, whereas independence gives 0.95^104≈0.00482230805327.
theorem_proof: The upper bound follows because the intersection is a subset of every A_i. For the lower bound apply the union bound to the failure events: P(∩A_i)=1−P(∪A_iᶜ)≥1−Σ(1−p_i). Probabilities are also nonnegative. The product formula follows only after imposing mutual independence. To see why pairwise independence is insufficient, let X,Y be independent fair bits and set Z=X xor Y. Any pair is independent, but P(X=Y=Z=1)=0 rather than 1/8.

For a zero case let failures be arcs of length 0.05 on the unit circle, starting at i/104. Since adjacent starts are less than 0.05 apart, the arcs cover the circle, so at least one failure always occurs, although each event still succeeds with probability 0.95. Independent Bernoulli variables give the intermediate product.","conclusion":"The same individual accuracy is compatible with no chance of complete correctness, a 95 percent chance, or the independent-model value. Replacing a dependency model by repeated multiplication can therefore be a major modeling error even after arithmetic is repaired."}

title: Nonlinearity does not imply chaos or identifiability
revised_question: Which state variables, conservation laws, observation map and parameter regime support a claimed mechanism or chaotic behavior?
status: Classical result developed and example checked
summary: A rigorous counterexample is more informative than another catalogue of nonlinear applications. A simple nonlinear ODE has a fully solvable, globally convergent flow and an observation that permanently hides the sign of its initial state.
definitions_json: ["Consider ẋ=−x³ on the real line for t≥0. The state is x, and first choose the observable y=x².","An observation model is identifiable on a set if no two admissible initial states generate exactly the same observed time history. This is distinct from state stability."]

With V=x²/2, V̇=−x⁴≤0, and the explicit solution proves convergence. Squaring removes the initial sign for all times. Equivalently y satisfies ẏ=−2y² with the same initial y₀ for both states. Thus the nonlinear system is elementary and convergent, while the chosen observation remains structurally ambiguous.

No increase in temporal sampling resolves the sign because the entire continuous histories coincide. Adding the observable z=x distinguishes the two immediately. The exact rational y values and the observation evolution equation are checked by the verifier.","conclusion":"Complexity of the evolution law, richness of sampling and distinguishability of states are separate questions. This example refutes a generic inference from nonlinear equations to chaos and a generic inference from many measurements to complete state reconstruction."}

title: The Klein–Gordon dispersion relation and its massless limit

Multiplying by ℏ² and writing E=ℏω and p=ℏk gives E²=c²|p|²+m²c⁴. For m>0, differentiating the positive branch gives group velocity v_g=c²k/ω with magnitude below c; at high frequency it approaches c. These are consequences of the chosen PDE and Fourier ansatz, not additional quantum postulates.

title: A controlled formal route from Dirac to Pauli

Since [π_i,π_j]=iqℏε_ijkB_k, the second term is −qℏσ·B. Inserting this identity into the first equation produces the Hamiltonian and fixes the sign convention.

title: Maxwell equations as field equations and identities

The local converse dF=0⇒F=dA is the Poincaré lemma under the contractibility assumption. It is not a global theorem on arbitrary manifolds: nontrivial degree-two cohomology can obstruct a single globally defined potential. The coordinate form of dF=0 is the homogeneous Maxwell system; the Hodge-star equation contains the metric-dependent dynamical content.

Adding dχ for χ=λtx changes components of A but contributes no change to F.","conclusion":"The example distinguishes the automatic homogeneous identity, the dispersion imposed by the vacuum field equation and a gauge change of the potential. It also shows why covariant notation alone is not a quantization procedure."}

title: Moving level sets and the singularity of threshold coordinates
revised_question: When does the threshold define a smooth boundary, and what fails when the spatial derivative vanishes?
status: Classical result developed and example checked
summary: An implicit boundary can be differentiated only where its defining level is regular. The same calculation quantifies sensitivity and gives an exact example where a boundary is born and its graph velocity diverges.
definitions_json: ["Let f(x,t) be continuously differentiable and consider the level set f(x,t)=c. A regular spatial level has ∇ₓf≠0.","For a one-dimensional graph r(t), the condition is f_r(r(t),t)≠0. Choose the unit normal n=∇f/|∇f| when discussing normal velocity."]

For the perturbation, Taylor-expand f(X+δr n,t)+δf=c and use ∇f·n=|∇f|. The denominator therefore measures conditioning as well as existence of the local graph. Tangential motion is a parametrization choice and is not fixed by the level equation.

At t=0 the spatial gradient vanishes at the origin. For t<0 there is no real level set, at zero there is one point, and for t>0 there is a circle. The one-dimensional version r²−t=0 has two branches ±sqrt(t), neither a differentiable graph through the critical event.","conclusion":"The diverging speed is not a contradiction in the implicit-function theorem; it occurs exactly where its nonzero-gradient hypothesis fails. Concentration measures amount per volume, whereas the supplied spatial quantity is an area. Their product has amount per length, so an amount cannot be inferred without a depth or volume model. The molar conversion at the end can be correct while the preceding quantity is ill-defined. This entry develops only the mathematics of that error, not an environmental prescription.

title: Stored energy needs a state function and a power balance
revised_question: Reconstruction: What extra state relation is needed to turn charge into an energy quantity, and how does a specified lumped model account for delivered power and loss?
status: Developed mathematical repair with exact worked checks; historical evidence is assistant-only
summary: This entry is a new mathematical reconstruction of a recovered qualitative concept. The source does not contain the equations below. The useful correction is to distinguish charge, voltage, energy and power instead of treating a carrier count or a metaphor as an energy calculation. A simple declared state model is enough to show what information a quantitative answer would require.
definitions_json: ["Charge q is measured in coulombs, current I in coulombs per second, voltage in joules per coulomb, energy in joules and power in joules per second.","Let q∈[0,Q] denote remaining charge. Prescribe a continuous open-circuit voltage function V_oc(q) and define the model storage function E(q)=∫_0^q V_oc(s)ds.","For discharge take I(t)≥0, qdot=−I, resistance R≥0 and terminal voltage V(t)=V_oc(q(t))−RI(t). This is a stated lumped model, not a complete electrochemical description."]

theorem_statement: Along an absolutely continuous charge trajectory with integrable power terms, Edot=−V_oc(q)I almost everywhere. Therefore Edot+P_out+P_loss=0 with P_out=VI and P_loss=RI². Charge capacity Q alone does not determine stored energy: the voltage-state law is also required.

A closed ball and its boundary sphere behave differently, and even-dimensional spheres have a parity obstruction absent on S¹. A fully labeled small simplex therefore exists. Let its mesh tend to zero and choose a convergent subsequence of its vertices using compactness. Continuity gives xᵢ≥Fᵢ(x) for every i at the common limiting point. Equal coordinate sums force equality in all coordinates, giving a fixed point. This proof uses Sperner’s lemma as a stated classical combinatorial input. For hairy ball, suppose a nowhere-zero tangent field exists and normalize it to w(x). Then H(x,t)=cos(πt)x+sin(πt)w(x) stays on S² because x and w are orthogonal unit vectors. It is a homotopy from id to −id, contradicting their different degrees. This proves the obstruction using the stated degree facts.

summary: For γ≥0, the optimum is min(γ,1). The true split 00|11 is uniquely optimal as an unlabeled partition for γ<1; the one-cluster partition is uniquely optimal for γ>1; both tie at γ=1. theorem_name: Spatial coherence gives an exact cut-versus-fit threshold
theorem_statement: For γ≥0, the optimum is min(γ,1). The true split 00|11 is uniquely optimal as an unlabeled partition for γ<1; the one-cluster partition is uniquely optimal for γ>1; both tie at γ=1.
theorem_proof: The all-equal partition has cut zero and W=1. Every nonconstant labeling on a connected path has at least one cut and W≥0, so its objective is at least γ. The labeling (0,0,1,1) has one cut and W=0, attaining that lower bound. For γ<1 it beats the constant partition. Equality in the nonconstant lower bound requires W=0, so no cluster can mix a zero and a one. With at most two clusters this forces exactly the split by value. For γ>1, every nonconstant partition has objective at least γ>1. The same argument gives only the two stated optima at equality; exhaustive enumeration independently checks the finite certificate.

Multiplying every observation by c multiplies W by c² but leaves cut unchanged, moving the threshold to γ=c².","conclusion":"Spatial regularization is a tunable mathematical preference with a measurable failure mode. limits: The proof uses this path, these observations and at most two clusters. More labels, normalized cuts, weighted edges or higher-dimensional data create different thresholds. A continuum perimeter limit needs additional scaling assumptions.
extension: On a larger finite graph, retain each partition’s pair (cut,W). Lower supporting lines of these points determine all parameter transitions. Dominated pairs can be discarded, yielding a compact exact certificate of the regularization path.

title: Three regularizers produce three different shrinkage rules
revised_question: Does the model penalize an ℓ₁ norm, an ℓ₂ norm or a squared ℓ₂ norm, and what solution does that choice actually imply?
status: Corrected formulation or classical result with an explicit worked example
summary: The solutions are componentwise soft threshold x_i=sign(z_i)max(|z_i|−λ,0), radial shrink x=max(1−λ/||z||₂,0)z, and ridge x=z/(1+λ), respectively. Writing ||M||₂ without stating whether M is a vector or a matrix is incomplete: a matrix spectral norm, Frobenius norm and entrywise norm lead to different optimization problems.
definitions_json: ["Fix z∈Rⁿ and λ>0. Strict convexity of the quadratic term gives a unique minimizer for each convex penalty.","The ℓ₁ penalty is λΣ|x_i|. The unsquared ℓ₂ penalty is λ√Σx_i². Ridge uses λ||x||₂²/2.","A subgradient g of a convex function f at x satisfies f(y)≥f(x)+gᵀ(y−x) for every y."]
theorem_name: Three regularizers produce three different shrinkage rules
theorem_statement: The solutions are componentwise soft threshold x_i=sign(z_i)max(|z_i|−λ,0), radial shrink x=max(1−λ/||z||₂,0)z, and ridge x=z/(1+λ), respectively.
theorem_proof: For ℓ₁ the coordinates separate. At a positive coordinate, optimality gives x_i−z_i+λ=0; at a negative one it gives x_i−z_i−λ=0. At zero, the subgradient interval [−λ,λ] contains z_i exactly when |z_i|≤λ. For the unsquared ℓ₂ norm and a nonzero solution, x−z+λx/||x||=0, so x points along z and its length is ||z||−λ. At zero, optimality requires z in the radius-λ Euclidean ball, giving the threshold case. Ridge is differentiable everywhere: x−z+λx=0. These conditions are sufficient by convexity and unique by strict convexity of the full objective.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Use z=(3,4), λ=1, and then a small first coordinate z=(1/2,4).","calculation":"For (3,4), soft threshold gives (2,3); radial shrink gives (12/5,16/5), since ||z||=5; ridge gives (3/2,2). For (1/2,4), ℓ₁ sets the first coordinate exactly to zero, while both other rules retain a nonzero first coordinate. Thus sparsity of individual coefficients follows from a specific corner geometry rather than from the generic word regularization.","conclusion":"Writing ||M||₂ without stating whether M is a vector or a matrix is incomplete: a matrix spectral norm, Frobenius norm and entrywise norm lead to different optimization problems."}
limits: The derivation concerns an identity quadratic data term. Replacing it with ||Ax−z||² generally destroys the coordinatewise closed form. It does not establish that any penalty identifies a scientifically correct model.
extension: For disjoint groups of coefficients, Σ_g||x_g||₂ yields one radial threshold per group. This keeps or removes entire groups and provides a precise intermediate choice between coordinate sparsity and uniform ridge shrinkage. Each of these proximal maps is nonexpansive: if outputs x,y correspond to inputs z,w, monotonicity of the convex subgradient gives〈(z−x)−(w−y),x−y〉≥0. Hence||x−y||²≤〈z−w,x−y〉≤||z−w||||x−y||, proving the unit Lipschitz bound.

title: An online centroid is a mean only for the right step sizes
revised_question: When is C_new=C_old+η(x_new−C_old) the sample mean, and when is it an exponentially weighted filter?
status: Corrected formulation or classical result with an explicit worked example
summary: With η_n=1/n and c₁=x₁, c_n=(x₁+⋯+x_n)/n. With constant η, c_n=rⁿc₀+ηΣ_{j=1}ⁿr^{n−j}x_j, E c_n=μ+rⁿ(c₀−μ), and Var(c_n)=ησ²(1−r^{2n})/(2−η). The update now has an explicit statistical interpretation and a calculable adaptation-versus-noise tradeoff.

Assignment of new points to a cluster is a separate problem from this update.","For the variance statement assume scalar independent x_n with common mean μ and variance σ², and a deterministic initial c₀.","For constant η define r=1−η. A forgetting factor r near one remembers more observations but adapts more slowly."]
theorem_name: An online centroid is a mean only for the right step sizes
theorem_statement: With η_n=1/n and c₁=x₁, c_n=(x₁+⋯+x_n)/n. With constant η, c_n=rⁿc₀+ηΣ_{j=1}ⁿr^{n−j}x_j, E c_n=μ+rⁿ(c₀−μ), and Var(c_n)=ησ²(1−r^{2n})/(2−η).
theorem_proof: The mean formula follows by induction after multiplying the recurrence by n. For constant η, repeated substitution gives the geometric expansion. Taking expectations and using ηΣ_{k=0}^{n−1}r^k=1−rⁿ yields the bias formula. Independence eliminates covariance cross terms, so variance is η²σ²Σ_{k=0}^{n−1}r^{2k}. Summing the geometric series and using 1−r²=η(2−η) gives the stated result. Its positive limit ησ²/(2−η) shows that fixed-step smoothing is not a consistent estimator of a static mean as n tends to infinity, although tracking a changing mean may motivate it.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Start at c₀=0 and feed the sequence 0,0,9 with constant η=1/2.","calculation":"The final value is 9/2, whereas the exact sample mean is three. Their disagreement is intentional weighting, not floating-point error. Under independent unit-variance observations the asymptotic filter variance is 1/3. limits: Cluster memberships selected from the same observations introduce selection and dependence; the elementary iid calculation no longer applies unchanged. Large steps or changing units can also change practical stability.
extension: For a deterministic drifting mean μ_n, the expected error satisfies e_n=(1−η)e_{n−1}+(1−η)(μ_{n−1}−μ_n). Solve this forced recurrence to bound tracking lag from a stated drift bound rather than describing the algorithm as universally adaptive. Matching the stationary variance with the varianceσ²/n of an equally weighted mean gives an effective sample size n_eff=(2−η)/η. Atη=1/2 this is three, even after infinitely many observations. This is a variance comparison under the iid model, not a count of actual retained records.

title: A similarity becomes a kernel only after a positivity check
revised_question: Which proposed similarity admits a Euclidean feature representation, and how can an invalid choice be rejected finitely?
status: Corrected formulation or classical result with an explicit worked example
summary: For scalar x,y, k(x,y)=(1+xy)² is PSD, with φ(x)=(1,√2x,x²). By contrast k_bad(x,y)=1−xy fails PSD even on the two points −1 and one. This separates a computable mathematical certificate from the informal description quantum-inspired or nonlinear.

This is a direct certificate, valid for arbitrary finite samples.","Symmetry alone does not imply positivity, and a positive entrywise table need not be a PSD matrix."]
theorem_name: A similarity becomes a kernel only after a positivity check
theorem_statement: For scalar x,y, k(x,y)=(1+xy)² is PSD, with φ(x)=(1,√2x,x²). By contrast k_bad(x,y)=1−xy fails PSD even on the two points −1 and one.
theorem_proof: Expand the polynomial: (1+xy)²=1+2xy+x²y², equal to the stated dot product. The norm-square identity proves positivity without requiring an eigenvalue calculation for each dataset. For the counterexample, the diagonal values at ±1 are zero and the off-diagonal values are two. Thus K_bad=[[0,2],[2,0]]. Taking a=(1,−1) gives aᵀK_bada=−4. This is a complete obstruction to a real Hilbert-space feature map with that similarity. A kernel used inside a quadratic objective needs its positivity assumptions checked before convexity or Euclidean geometry is inferred.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Use x=(−1,0,1) for the valid kernel, and x=(−1,1) for the invalid one.","calculation":"The valid Gram matrix is [[4,1,0],[1,1,1],[0,1,4]], whose leading principal determinants are four, three and eight. Even its nonnegative entries cannot rescue the missing PSD property.","conclusion":"This separates a computable mathematical certificate from the informal description quantum-inspired or nonlinear."}
limits: Finite positive tests cannot prove a proposed formula is PSD on every possible sample; the explicit feature map does. Conversely one finite negative test is decisive. Matrix rounding can require tolerances, but the supplied examples use exact integers.

title: Bayesian uncertainty and data fusion depend on covariance
revised_question: How does an explicit probabilistic model combine observations, and why can duplicated evidence not count as independent precision?
status: Corrected formulation or classical result with an explicit worked example
summary: The posterior variance and mean are v=(v₀⁻¹+nσ⁻²)⁻¹ and m=v(m₀/v₀+Σy_i/σ²). If Y consists of n identical copies of a single noisy measurement, Σ=σ²11ᵀ and every unbiased weighted estimate has variance σ², not σ²/n. Fusion quality depends on dependence structure as much as on the number of input channels.
definitions_json: ["Let θ∼N(m₀,v₀) and y_i|θ be independent N(θ,σ²). Precision is reciprocal variance.","For a linear estimate wᵀY with E Y=θ1, unbiasedness is wᵀ1=1 and variance is wᵀΣw.","A posterior variance describes uncertainty under a stated model. It is not a model-free confidence guarantee."]
theorem_name: Bayesian uncertainty and data fusion depend on covariance
theorem_statement: The posterior variance and mean are v=(v₀⁻¹+nσ⁻²)⁻¹ and m=v(m₀/v₀+Σy_i/σ²). If Y consists of n identical copies of a single noisy measurement, Σ=σ²11ᵀ and every unbiased weighted estimate has variance σ², not σ²/n.
theorem_proof: The log posterior is, up to constants, −(θ−m₀)²/(2v₀)−Σ(y_i−θ)²/(2σ²). Collecting its quadratic and linear coefficients gives −(θ−m)²/(2v) plus a constant, which proves the update. A future independent observation adds σ² to the posterior predictive variance. For duplicated evidence, compute wᵀΣw=σ²(wᵀ1)²=σ². No choice of unbiased weights reduces it. Treating the n coordinates as independent replaces this singular covariance with σ²I and would manufacture precision absent from the observations.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take m₀=0,v₀=1,σ²=1 and two independent observations y₁=1,y₂=2. Contrast them with two copies of the same observation.","calculation":"The independent-data posterior is N(1,1/3); a new observation has predictive variance 4/3. For two duplicated unit-variance measurements the average retains variance one, whereas two independent ones would average to variance one half. The posterior based on one measurement copied twice should therefore use one likelihood contribution, giving variance one half under this prior, rather than one third.","conclusion":"Fusion quality depends on dependence structure as much as on the number of input channels."}
limits: The Gaussian formulas require their likelihood, prior and independence assumptions. Perfect duplication is an extreme example; partially correlated inputs need covariance estimation and can be ill-conditioned. Neither a narrow posterior nor a numerical fusion score alone establishes model adequacy.
extension: For positive-definite Σ, minimize wᵀΣw subject to wᵀ1=1. A Lagrange multiplier gives w=Σ⁻¹1/(1ᵀΣ⁻¹1) and variance 1/(1ᵀΣ⁻¹1). At singular Σ, solve on its supported subspace rather than substituting an inverse that does not exist.

title: Transfer learning needs a support and invariance assumption
revised_question: Under what assumptions can a source-domain loss estimate target-domain performance?
status: Corrected formulation or classical result with an explicit worked example
summary: Under the stated assumptions, R_T(f)=E_S[w(X)ℓ(f(X),Y)]. A region with positive target probability but zero source probability cannot be handled by finite importance weights. Its labels can change target risk without changing any source observations. The revised question exposes the mathematical assumptions behind an asserted benefit from transferring a model.
definitions_json: ["Let P_S and P_T be source and target joint distributions of (X,Y), with bounded loss ℓ(f(X),Y).","Covariate shift means P_T(Y|X)=P_S(Y|X) on relevant support, while the marginal distribution of X may differ.","If P_T^X is absolutely continuous with respect to P_S^X, let w=dP_T^X/dP_S^X. In a finite space this is the ratio of target to source probabilities."]
theorem_name: Transfer learning needs a support and invariance assumption
theorem_statement: Under the stated assumptions, R_T(f)=E_S[w(X)ℓ(f(X),Y)]. A region with positive target probability but zero source probability cannot be handled by finite importance weights. Its labels can change target risk without changing any source observations.
theorem_proof: Condition on X. Shared conditionals make the conditional expected loss g(X)=E[ℓ(f(X),Y)|X] the same in both domains. Then R_T=∫g dP_T^X=∫wg dP_S^X=E_S[wℓ]. This uses the Radon–Nikodym change of measure, not a claim that any transferred representation preserves the conditional law. For the obstruction, place all source mass at X=0 and all target mass at X=1. Two data-generating worlds can agree on the source label Y=0 at zero but assign opposite labels at one. Every source dataset is identically distributed in both worlds, while a fixed predictor has different target error. Source-only risk estimation cannot distinguish them.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Let X∈{0,1}, P_S=(3/4,1/4), P_T=(1/4,3/4), with Y=X and predictor f≡0 under zero-one loss.","calculation":"Source risk is 1/4 and target risk is 3/4. Weights are 1/3 at zero and three at one, so weighted source risk is (1/4)·3=3/4 exactly. The identity works because both target points occur in the source. It fails to supply an estimator in the support-gap example, where the required ratio at one has a zero denominator.","conclusion":"The revised question exposes the mathematical assumptions behind an asserted benefit from transferring a model."}
limits: This identity does not prove low variance of an empirical estimator, successful representation learning or unchanged conditionals. Large weights can make estimation unstable. Biological or other applied interpretations from the source are not inferred from the algebra.
extension: For losses in [0,1] and weights bounded by M, a simple second-moment bound is E_S[(wℓ)²]≤M E_S[w]=M. It quantifies one reason that overlap and controlled density ratios matter for reliable transfer.

title: PCA reconstruction rank is not intrinsic dimension
revised_question: Which dimension is measured by a covariance spectrum, and what information is changed by a neighborhood embedding?
status: Corrected formulation or classical result with an explicit worked example
summary: If eigenvalues areλ₁≥⋯≥λ_d≥0, the optimal rank-k linear reconstruction error isΣ_{j>k}λ_j. For the uniform unit circle,Σ=I/2; every rank-one projector leaves error1/2 despite the curve being one-dimensional. The revised question prevents a variance threshold or a visually compelling embedding from being reported as a theorem about intrinsic dimension.
definitions_json: ["For centered random X∈Rᵈ with covariance Σ, a rank-k orthogonal projector P reconstructs PX and has expected squared error E||X−PX||².","PCA chooses the projector onto k eigenvectors with largest covariance eigenvalues. Intrinsic dimension instead concerns a local parameterization or another explicitly stated nonlinear definition.","The uniform circle is X=(cosΘ,sinΘ) with Θ uniform on[0,2π). It has one angular parameter and a two-dimensional affine span."]
theorem_name: PCA reconstruction rank is not intrinsic dimension
theorem_statement: If eigenvalues areλ₁≥⋯≥λ_d≥0, the optimal rank-k linear reconstruction error isΣ_{j>k}λ_j. For the uniform unit circle,Σ=I/2; every rank-one projector leaves error1/2 despite the curve being one-dimensional.
theorem_proof: Expand E||X−PX||²=tr((I−P)Σ), using symmetry and idempotence of P. In an eigenbasis ofΣ, tr(PΣ)=Σλ_jp_jj, where0≤p_jj≤1 andΣp_jj=k. Moving weight from a smallerλ to a larger one cannot reduce this sum, so its maximum is the sum of the k largest eigenvalues. This proves the PCA claim directly. On the circle, angular averages of cos² and sin² are1/2 and the cross average is zero. Thus both eigenvalues are positive and equal, and every line loses exactly half the variance. Local angular charts nevertheless describe a one-dimensional smooth manifold.

Projection onto the x-axis gives errors0,1,0,1 and mean1/2; every other line has the same mean error. A discrete sample alone is not assigned a manifold dimension by this calculation; the continuous-circle model supplies that separate hypothesis.","conclusion":"The revised question prevents a variance threshold or a visually compelling embedding from being reported as a theorem about intrinsic dimension."}
limits: The historical fragment explicitly supplies PCA but not a complete dimension-estimation algorithm. The t-SNE comparison and circle example are newly authored development rather than recovered historical claims. A discrete point cloud needs a separate geometric model before a manifold dimension can be assigned.
extension: t-SNE minimizes a KL divergence between high- and low-dimensional neighborhood distributions. Analyze its actual objective and initialization when interpreting a display; neither exact global distance preservation nor uniqueness follows from minimizing that divergence.

title: Perimeter–area measures need units and an edge-count convention
revised_question: Which landscape statistic is invariant under changing length units, and which boundaries are counted in its perimeter?
status: Corrected formulation or classical result with an explicit worked example
summary: The scaling laws follow directly from length and area. For a rectangle with sides a,b, P/(4√A)=(a+b)/(2√ab)≥1, with equality exactly for a square. Boundary conventions can produce different values even on the same partition. The original LSI-like expression is retained as historical evidence, while the revised statistic explicitly defines its numerator and normalization.
definitions_json: ["Let P be perimeter measured in a declared length unit and A positive area in the corresponding squared unit.","PAR=P/A has units of inverse length. The square-normalized ratio P/(4√A) is dimensionless; a disk-based normalization uses a different constant.","When patches share edges, summing every patch perimeter counts a shared edge twice. A distinct-edge total counts it once, and an exterior perimeter omits it."]
theorem_name: Perimeter–area measures need units and an edge-count convention
theorem_statement: The scaling laws follow directly from length and area. For a rectangle with sides a,b, P/(4√A)=(a+b)/(2√ab)≥1, with equality exactly for a square. Boundary conventions can produce different values even on the same partition.
theorem_proof: Dilation sends a,b to sa,sb, so P′=sP,A′=s²A. The ratios then transform as stated. The rectangle inequality is equivalent to a+b≥2√ab, or (√a−√b)²≥0. Its value depends only on aspect ratio and not size. Now partition a 2×1 rectangle into two adjacent unit squares. The patch perimeter sum is eight, the distinct-edge total is seven and the exterior perimeter is six. Dividing any of these by 4√2 gives a different statistic. Therefore replacing a named index by an unqualified sum Σp_i can change its meaning even though the expression is dimensionless.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Use the two adjacent unit squares and then double all lengths.","calculation":"The three candidate shape ratios are √2,7/(4√2),3/(2√2), approximately1.4142,1.2374,1.0607. All stay unchanged after dilation. The exterior PAR changes from6/2=3 to12/8=3/2. Thus scale invariance and edge-count agreement are separate checks; passing one does not establish the other.","conclusion":"The original LSI-like expression is retained as historical evidence, while the revised statistic explicitly defines its numerator and normalization."}
limits: A continuum perimeter, a raster edge count and a vector-map boundary length need not converge identically under resolution changes. The inequality with square normalization is a rectangle statement; the Euclidean isoperimetric optimum among all shapes is a disk and uses a different constant.
extension: For a connected n-cell raster region, perimeter in cell units is4n−2e, where e counts shared internal cell edges. This exact combinatorial identity separates geometry from double counting and supplies a useful implementation certificate.

title: An undefined Ψ measure needs an actual transport law

status: Revised classical development with scoped worked result
summary: The surviving label does not define a mathematical theory. A precise replacement is to ask what a measurable coordinate transport preserves. title: Ψ mutual information and capacity need a channel
revised_question: What channel law and input constraint define the information quantity, and can a relabeling change it?
status: Revised classical development with scoped worked result
summary: A channel capacity is an optimization over input distributions for a declared conditional law. It cannot be obtained by attaching a new symbol to mutual information. theorem_statement: For Y=X⊕N, with N independent Bernoulli(ε), the capacity is1−h₂(ε) bits per use and is attained by a uniform input. Bijections of the input or output alphabet preserve mutual information and capacity when the channel is transported consistently.

title: Functorial relabeling does not automatically preserve code distance

status: Revised classical development with scoped worked result
summary: A genuine categorical transport can preserve every composition law while changing the usual Hamming distance of a code. This small counterexample separates structural equivalence from a coding guarantee. It also explains why naming a category cannot supply a cryptographic hardness assumption: additional metric or computational structure must be part of the objects and morphisms.

theorem_statement: The transported maps preserve identity and composition. An ambient Hamming isometry is sufficient to preserve every code’s pairwise distances and minimum distance; transporting the metric also preserves all distances. Preserving every ambient pairwise distance is exactly the isometry condition. A non-isometric map may nevertheless preserve a particular code or its minimum distance.
theorem_proof: For composable f and g, (ψ_Zgψ_Y⁻¹)(ψ_Yfψ_X⁻¹)=ψ_Z(gf)ψ_X⁻¹. Transporting an identity gives an identity. Define d_ψ(ψx,ψy)=d_H(x,y); this pulled-back metric preserves distances tautologically. Keeping the old coordinate Hamming metric instead imposes the nontrivial condition d_H(ψx,ψy)=d_H(x,y). Composition preservation alone says nothing about that equality. Consequently a theorem about one category of sets cannot silently be interpreted as an equivalence of metric-code objects.

title: Euler’s product yields an exact partition recurrence
revised_question: Which generating series counts partitions, and what exact coefficient recurrence follows from Euler’s identity?
status: Revised classical development with scoped worked result
summary: A precise generating-function calculation is a much stronger result than a broad application list. definitions_json: ["Work in the formal ring Z[[q]], where each coefficient of an infinite product depends on finitely many factors. Let p(n) count unrestricted partitions, with p(0)=1 and p(n)=0 for n<0. Its generating series is P(q)=∏_{m≥1}(1−q^m)⁻¹."]
theorem_name: Pentagonal recurrence with formal-series scope
theorem_statement: Euler’s classical identity ∏_{m≥1}(1−q^m)=Σ_{k∈Z}(−1)^kq^{k(3k−1)/2} implies p(n)=Σ_{k≥1}(−1)^(k−1)[p(n−k(3k−1)/2)+p(n−k(3k+1)/2)]. Each coefficient equation is finite.

Multiply Euler’s identity by P to obtain one. For n>0, its nth coefficient is zero; isolate the k=0 term p(n), pair positive and negative k, and move the remaining terms to the other side. Formal finiteness follows because the pentagonal exponents grow quadratically. This argument derives the recurrence from the stated classical theorem, rather than pretending a finite coefficient test proves the entire Euler identity.

title: Gradient-flow curvature is a projected Hessian quantity

status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example

theorem_statement: κ=|P_{g⊥}Hg|/|g|². In particular κ≤||H||/|g|. If V is μ-strongly convex, its gap along the flow satisfies V(x(t))−V_*≤e^{−2μt}(V(x(0))−V_*).

Tangential Hessian action changes speed; only its perpendicular component bends the curve. For decay, strong convexity implies V_*≥V(x)+g·(x_*−x)+(μ/2)|x_*−x|². theorem_proof: Differentiate q to obtain g+(H+η⁻¹I)δ=0. Positive definiteness makes this system invertible and its stationary point the unique global minimum. Diagonalize H orthogonally to obtain each scalar formula. Completing the square with A=H+η⁻¹I gives q(δ)=.5(δ+A⁻¹g)ᵀA(δ+A⁻¹g)−.5gᵀA⁻¹g, yielding the minimum. For λ_i≥0, every damping factor 1/(1+ηλ_i) lies in (0,1], proving the norm bound. These statements concern the quadratic model; actual objective decrease requires an upper-model or remainder condition.

The stiff second direction is reduced by a factor of ten. If instead λ₁=−1 at η=1, the first quadratic coefficient vanishes and a nonzero g₁ makes the model unbounded below, so the apparent infinite update signals a failed assumption.","conclusion":"The formula is a checked optimization theorem rather than an automatic mode-elimination principle."}

title: Hypergeometric face survival gives an exact expected Euler characteristic
revised_question: How does uniform fixed-size vertex sampling transform the Euler characteristic of a finite complex?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: Each simplex survives exactly when all of its vertices are sampled, giving a hypergeometric inclusion probability. Linearity of expectation then yields an exact polynomial transform of the face counts, without pretending that the alternating sum recovers a barcode.
definitions_json: ["Let K be a finite abstract simplicial complex on N vertices and f_{b−1} its number of faces with b vertices.","Choose an m-element vertex subset S uniformly and let K[S] contain exactly the faces of K whose vertices lie in S.","Use ordinary Euler characteristic χ(K[S])=∑_{b≥1}(−1)^{b−1}f_{b−1}(K[S]); the empty complex has χ=0."]
theorem_name: Exact fixed-size sampling identity
theorem_statement: Eχ(K[S])=∑_{b≥1}(−1)^{b−1}f_{b−1}·C(m,b)/C(N,b), with the ratio zero for b>m. For independent vertex retention probability p the corresponding formula is ∑(−1)^{b−1}f_{b−1}p^b.
theorem_proof: Write the random face count as a sum of indicators over the original faces. A fixed b-vertex face lies in exactly C(N−b,m−b) of the C(N,m) possible samples. Their ratio equals C(m,b)/C(N,b) by factorial cancellation. Taking expectations and the alternating sum proves the identity; independence between faces is unnecessary. Under independent retention, a face’s inclusion probability is p^b instead. For fixed b and m/N=ρ bounded away from zero, expanding the product ∏_{j=0}^{b−1}(m−j)/(N−j) gives log Π=b log ρ−(1−ρ)b(b−1)/(2ρN)+O(N^{−2}); the constant may depend on b and the lower bound on ρ. In dimension three this becomes f₀p−f₁p²+f₂p³−f₃p⁴, with the same hypergeometric replacement for fixed-size sampling. This is an exact finite identity, not an asymptotic density argument.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take K to be the four-cycle graph, with N=4 and four edges, and sample m=2 vertices.","calculation":"There are six samples. Four adjacent pairs induce an edge with χ=1; two opposite pairs induce isolated vertices with χ=2. Their mean is (4+4)/6=4/3. The formula gives 4·(2/4)−4·(1/6)=4/3. For m=3 each sample is a three-vertex path and χ=1.","conclusion":"The full finite distribution checks the expectation and reveals the variability hidden by its mean."}
limits: The same Euler characteristic can arise from different Betti numbers and different persistence intervals. A real geographic dataset or operational benefit is not established by this identity; the retrieved source explicitly reported no dataset execution.
extension: Derive the variance by classifying pairs of faces according to their union size, using their joint survival probability C(m,|σ∪τ|)/C(N,|σ∪τ|). Determine which additional observations identify Betti curves beyond the Euler projection.
references_json: [{"label":"Herbert Edelsbrunner and John Harer, Persistent Homology—A Survey","url":"https://doi.org/10.1090/conm/453/08802"}]

title: Random birth times connect order statistics to an exact barcode law
revised_question: When can the birth distribution of a persistent cycle be derived exactly from its support?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: A four-cycle with independent vertex arrival times gives a complete random persistence interval. The example distinguishes a necessary support-survival law from claims about arbitrary cycle detection, where alternative representatives and earlier fillings change the answer.
definitions_json: ["Give each vertex of a four-cycle an independent Uniform[0,1] birth time U_i. An edge enters when both its endpoints have arrived.","At time one, add one diagonal and the two triangles filling the square. Before that time the filtration contains only the induced cycle graph.","Work with homology over a field. Let B=max(U₁,U₂,U₃,U₄)."]
theorem_name: A random interval and its expected length
theorem_statement: Almost surely the degree-one barcode consists of the single interval [B,1). Its birth cumulative distribution is P(B≤t)=t⁴ for 0≤t≤1, expected length is 1/5, and the expected first Betti number is t⁴ for 0≤t<1.
theorem_proof: Before all four vertices arrive, every induced subgraph is a forest and therefore has H₁=0. Once they all arrive, the full cycle is present and has one independent cycle because m−n+1=1. At time one the two triangles and their diagonal form a disk, killing that class. Independence gives P(B≤t)=∏P(U_i≤t)=t⁴. Its density is 4t³, hence E B=∫₀¹4t⁴dt=4/5 and E(1−B)=1/5. Alternatively the layer-cake identity gives expected bar length ∫₀¹P(B≤t)dt=1/5. These two calculations independently connect a random barcode with its expected Betti curve.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Compare observation at t=1/2 with sampling exactly three of the four vertices.","calculation":"Under independent arrival, the cycle has appeared with probability (1/2)⁴=1/16 at t=.5. Under a uniform three-vertex sample the cycle is never present. For a uniform m-element subset of a larger N-vertex system, a specified b-vertex support survives with probability C(m,b)/C(N,b), agreeing with the separate hypergeometric formula.","conclusion":"A fully declared filtration permits an exact persistence distribution rather than a generic random-barcode slogan."}
limits: In a larger complex, a homology class may have several representatives or be filled before all vertices of a chosen support arrive. Support inclusion is then not automatically equivalent to persistence detection.
extension: For a supplied complex, enumerate minimal cycle supports and fillings, use inclusion–exclusion for alternative representatives, and derive a confidence bound for detecting every bar longer than a stated threshold.
references_json: [{"label":"Afra Zomorodian and Gunnar Carlsson, Computing Persistent Homology","url":"https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-004-1146-y"}]

title: Weighted sampling replaces hypergeometric ratios by symmetric polynomials
revised_question: How do nonuniform fixed-size sampling weights change face survival probabilities?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: A product-weight distribution on subsets has an elementary-symmetric normalizer. This yields an exact inclusion law and a dynamic program for expected Euler characteristic, while clarifying that different without-replacement sampling schemes need not share this law.
definitions_json: ["Choose positive vertex weights w₁,…,w_N and a size m. Give an m-element subset S probability ∏_{i∈S}w_i/e_m(w), where e_m(w)=∑_{|S|=m}∏_{i∈S}w_i.","For a fixed vertex set F of size b, let w_{Fᶜ} denote the remaining weights and w_F=∏_{i∈F}w_i.","This is a specified subset distribution, not an assertion about sequential probability-proportional-to-size draws."]
theorem_name: Exact weighted inclusion and an O(Nm) normalizer
theorem_statement: P(F⊂S)=w_F e_{m−b}(w_{Fᶜ})/e_m(w), for b≤m. Consequently expected Euler characteristic is the alternating sum of these probabilities over the faces. The e_r can be computed by E_{j,r}=E_{j−1,r}+w_jE_{j−1,r−1}.
theorem_proof: Every subset containing F is uniquely F∪T with T⊂Fᶜ and |T|=m−b. Summing its product weight factors out w_F and leaves the elementary symmetric polynomial in the complement. Dividing by the original normalizer proves the formula. To derive the recurrence, split r-element subsets of the first j vertices into those omitting j and those containing it. Initialize E_{0,0}=1 and E_{0,r}=0 for r>0. Updating r in descending order uses O(m) storage and O(Nm) arithmetic operations. Equal weights give e_m=C(N,m)w^m and recover the uniform hypergeometric probability exactly.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take weights (1,2,3), m=2, and a graph with only the edge {1,2}.","calculation":"The three subset weights are 2,3,6, so e₂=11. Vertex inclusion probabilities are 5/11,8/11,9/11 and sum to two, as required by fixed sample size. The edge survives with probability 2/11. Thus Eχ=2−2/11=20/11, also obtained by averaging χ=1,2,2 against probabilities 2/11,3/11,6/11.","conclusion":"The weighted normalizer, all marginals and the topological statistic agree by independent enumeration."}
limits: Large or highly unequal weights require stable arithmetic or exact rational computation. The formula alone does not choose scientifically justified weights, guarantee unbiased inference about a population or preserve homology.
extension: Compute pairwise face inclusion probabilities and exact variance using complement symmetric polynomials. Investigate weight design under a fixed budget to maximize detection of a declared family of cycle supports.

title: Empirical Fisher, Gauss–Newton and Hessian are different matrices
revised_question: Which curvature matrix does a gradient-outer-product routine estimate, and when does a spectral projection guarantee descent?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: A scalar squared-loss example separates three commonly conflated matrices exactly. An orthogonal projection has a precise first-order descent identity, while a finite Lanczos approximation needs an independently checked residual before its eigenpairs can be trusted.
definitions_json: ["For sample losses ℓ_i(θ), the empirical Fisher is F=n⁻¹∑g_ig_iᵀ, g_i=∇ℓ_i. It is positive semidefinite by construction.","For a scalar prediction f_θ and squared loss ℓ=(f_θ−y)²/2, the generalized Gauss–Newton matrix is G=JᵀJ, while the Hessian is G+(f_θ−y)∇²f_θ.","Let P be an orthogonal projector, so P=Pᵀ=P². Consider the update θ⁺=θ−ηP∇L(θ)."]
theorem_name: Curvature distinction and projected descent
theorem_statement: F,G and ∇²ℓ can differ even in one dimension. If L has M-Lipschitz gradient, then L(θ⁺)≤L(θ)−η(1−Mη/2)||P∇L||², so 0<η<2/M gives descent unless the projected gradient vanishes.
theorem_proof: Differentiating the squared loss gives g=(f−y)J and ∇²ℓ=JᵀJ+(f−y)∇²f; its outer product is (f−y)²JᵀJ, proving the distinction. For descent apply the smoothness inequality L(θ+v)≤L+gᵀv+(M/2)||v||² to v=−ηPg. Orthogonality gives gᵀPg=||Pg||² and ||v||²=η²||Pg||², yielding the result. If the projection discards the gradient entirely, the update is zero regardless of large retained eigenvalues. For a unit approximate eigenvector v of a symmetric matrix, residual ||Av−λv|| bounds the distance of λ to the true spectrum; expand v in an orthonormal eigenbasis to prove this immediately.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take f_θ=θ², y=1 and θ=0.","calculation":"Then J=0 and g=0, so empirical Fisher and GGN are both zero. But the Hessian is 2(3θ²−1)=−2 at zero, revealing negative curvature invisible to either PSD matrix. At θ=1, the exact-fit gradient and empirical Fisher vanish, whereas GGN and Hessian both equal four.","conclusion":"A metrics harness must label its operator and report what its approximation actually measures."}
limits: The projected-descent theorem is local smooth optimization, not a guarantee of lower perplexity, faster training or generalization. LoRA parametrization also changes which parameter-space matrix is being studied.
extension: Implement matrix-vector products for each declared curvature operator, verify symmetry and residuals, and compare projected updates at matched compute and learning-rate conditions. State the approximation subspace and retained gradient energy.

title: Genus-two point counts determine a Frobenius polynomial
revised_question: How do exact counts over F_p and F_{p²} reconstruct the genus-two local polynomial?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: Newton’s identities recover the middle coefficient from two point counts. A completely enumerated smooth hyperelliptic curve over F₃ supplies a certificate for the local polynomial, while global rank and endomorphism claims remain separate questions.
definitions_json: ["Let C/F_p be smooth projective of genus two and let N_r=#C(F_{p^r}). Its Frobenius eigenvalues α₁,…,α₄ satisfy N_r=p^r+1−∑α_i^r.","Write P_p(X)=∏(X−α_i)=X⁴−a₁X³+a₂X²−pa₁X+p². The reciprocal symmetry and |α_i|=√p are background Weil theorems for curves.","Use C:y²=x⁵−x+1 over F₃, with its unique point at infinity."]
theorem_name: Reconstruction and an exact finite-field example
theorem_statement: a₁=p+1−N₁ and a₂=[N₂−(p²+1)+a₁²]/2. For the displayed curve N₁=7 and N₂=15, giving P₃(X)=X⁴+3X³+7X²+9X+9.
theorem_proof: The first count gives ∑α_i=a₁. Newton’s identity ∑α_i²=a₁²−2a₂ combined with N₂ gives the formula. For smoothness, in F₃ the derivative of f=x⁵−x+1 is 2(x⁴+1). Dividing f by x⁴+1 leaves x+1, and x⁴+1 evaluated at −1 is two, so the gcd is one. An odd-degree squarefree degree-five hyperelliptic equation in odd characteristic has smooth projective genus two with one point at infinity. Enumerate x,y in F₃ and in F₉=F₃[u]/(u²+1), count y²=f(x) and add that infinity point; this gives the stated counts.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Inspect both the count and the Weil-size consistency.","calculation":"For x=0,1,2 in F₃, f(x)=1, so each x has two y values and N₁=6+1=7. Over F₉ exhaustive enumeration gives 14 affine points and one at infinity. The polynomial factors over R as (X²+aX+3)(X²+bX+3), with a,b=(3±√5)/2. Both |a|,|b|<2√3, so each quadratic has conjugate roots of modulus √3.","conclusion":"The exact point enumeration and independent root-size check support the local arithmetic calculation. The constant coefficient p² and reciprocal linear coefficient encode the genus-two duality symmetry, so checking only the first trace would leave necessary polynomial data undetermined."}
limits: This does not prove a global Mordell–Weil rank formula, a Sato–Tate law, BSD or a Jacobian endomorphism classification. Those require global data and additional theorems.
extension: Count over more good primes, compute exact polynomial discriminants and splitting patterns, and compare candidate endomorphism algebras using rigorous exclusion criteria rather than numerical resemblance alone.

title: Swan conductor measures ramification rather than vector-space rank
revised_question: What does the displayed Swan-conductor sum measure, and why is it not an automatic additive decomposition of arithmetic rank?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: A one-dimensional representation with a wild ramification break gives an explicit conductor while its dimension remains one. This separates a valid local invariant from an undefined global rank decomposition and records the exact hypotheses behind the sum.
definitions_json: ["Let L/K be a finite Galois extension of local fields, G₀ its inertia group and G_i its lower-numbered ramification groups for i≥1.","For a finite-dimensional characteristic-zero representation V, define Sw(V)=∑_{i≥1}|G_i|/|G₀|·codim V^{G_i}.","The Artin conductor is codim V^{G₀}+Sw(V). Only finitely many terms are nonzero because the ramification filtration eventually becomes trivial."]
theorem_name: A one-dimensional wild-break calculation
theorem_statement: If G₀=G₁=…=G_b=C_p and G_{b+1}=1, and V is a nontrivial one-dimensional character of C_p, then dim V=1, Sw(V)=b and its Artin conductor is b+1. A nontrivial tame character has Swan conductor zero.
theorem_proof: For every 1≤i≤b the group acts nontrivially on the one-dimensional space, so V^{G_i}=0 and its codimension is one. The index factor |G_i|/|G₀| is also one. Summing b terms gives b. At i>b the acting group is trivial and the codimension is zero. Inertia invariants are zero, adding one to the Artin conductor. For a tame character the wild groups G_i, i≥1, act trivially, hence every term vanishes even though inertia itself may act nontrivially. Additivity of invariant codimensions under direct sums gives conductor additivity, which is a different statement from an additive formula for a global arithmetic rank.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Use a characteristic-two Artin–Schreier model y²−y=t^{−3} over F₂((t)).","calculation":"Its standard ramification theorem gives a single lower break b=3 for the nontrivial character. The preceding calculation then yields dimension one, Swan conductor three and Artin conductor four. The break theorem is cited background; the conductor sum itself is explicit once that filtration is specified.","conclusion":"Dimension and ramification can vary independently, so each term in a proposed rank identity needs a separate definition and theorem."}
limits: The retrieved λ+κ+ΣSw+δ_tor expression does not define its terms sufficiently to establish a universal rank formula. The example does not claim to prove the general ramification-break theorem from scratch.
extension: For a supplied local representation, compute the ramification filtration and fixed spaces, then compare conductor contributions with an actual global Euler–Poincaré formula or Selmer exact sequence under their full hypotheses.

title: A fund target is an annuity recurrence with explicit assumptions
revised_question: What contribution stream would reach a specified nominal target under a constant-return model?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: An exact linear recurrence separates contributions, assumed returns and payouts. It turns the historical numerical target into a transparent mathematical scenario, without treating a proposed allocation or future return as established fact.
definitions_json: ["Let W_n be a fund balance after year n, W₀=0, r a constant net annual return and c a constant contribution paid at year end. Use W_{n+1}=(1+r)W_n+c.","Assume r>−1 and specify that all values are nominal. Fees, inflation and uncertain returns are absent unless introduced explicitly.","For a monthly payout D to P recipients, the annual payout is 12DP, a flow with different units from the asset stock."]
theorem_name: Exact target and payout arithmetic
theorem_statement: For r≠0, W_n=c[(1+r)^n−1]/r; at r=0 it equals nc. A target T at year n requires c=Tr/[(1+r)^n−1]. A balance by itself does not determine a sustainable payout.
theorem_proof: Iterate the recurrence to get c∑_{j=0}^{n−1}(1+r)^j and sum the geometric series. The r→0 limit is n by the derivative of (1+r)^n. If a fixed annual payout b is also made, replace c by c−b in the same recurrence; a nonnegative nominal equilibrium under this simplified accounting needs inflow plus modeled return to cover b. For variable returns, the exact balance is a weighted sum of contributions multiplied by subsequent return products, so order and volatility matter. Neither an expected return nor a portfolio percentage makes the constant-r path certain.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take T=10 trillion units and n=20.","calculation":"At r=0 the required yearly contribution is .5 trillion. At the explicitly hypothetical r=.05, it is about .302426 trillion because 1.05²⁰≈2.653298. For P=100 million, monthly D=200 costs .24 trillion annually, while D=800 costs .96 trillion. These are arithmetic flows, not forecasts of affordable distributions.","conclusion":"The target, horizon, contribution timing and payout denominator are all visible in the calculation."}
limits: This entry supplies no investment recommendation or prediction. Inflation, taxes, risk, demographics and changes in contributions can materially alter the model; historical policy targets remain proposals.
extension: Replace constant r by a stated stochastic return model, derive the distribution of terminal wealth and shortfall probability, and compare real rather than nominal targets with an explicit inflation process.

title: Compatibility and gluing can be tested by a linear obstruction
revised_question: What explicit obstruction distinguishes local consistency from a globally compatible assignment?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: Differences prescribed on graph edges glue to vertex potentials exactly when their cycle sums vanish. This finite model gives a complete obstruction theory and clarifies when a rank-sized witness is merely linear redundancy rather than a theorem translating every mathematical branch.
definitions_json: ["Let B be the oriented incidence matrix of a connected finite graph. An edge datum a∈R^m is compatible with vertex potentials when a=Bᵀx for some x∈R^n.","A cycle vector c satisfies Bc=0. The obstruction functional is cᵀa.","For a finite collection of row vectors A_W, define r(W) as the least number of selected rows with the same row-space rank."]
theorem_name: Cycle obstruction criterion and minimal linear witness
theorem_statement: The edge data glue if and only if cᵀa=0 for every cycle c. The solution is unique up to an additive constant. Moreover r(W)=rank(A_W), provided individual rows may be chosen freely.
theorem_proof: The orthogonal complement of im Bᵀ is ker B, since ⟨Bᵀx,c⟩=⟨x,Bc⟩. In finite-dimensional Euclidean space taking orthogonal complements again proves im Bᵀ=(ker B)⊥, giving necessity and sufficiency. If two potentials solve the equations their difference lies in ker Bᵀ, which consists of constants by connectivity. For r(W), any r selected rows have rank at most r, establishing the lower bound. A basis of the full row space can be selected from its spanning rows by Gaussian elimination, attaining the bound. This proves the source’s witness-size expression in its linear setting; nonlinear or constrained witnesses can behave differently.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Orient a triangle as 1→2→3→1 and prescribe edge increments (2,3,−5).","calculation":"The unique cycle sum is 2+3−5=0. Taking x₁=0 gives x₂=2 and x₃=5, and the final edge requires x₁−x₃=−5, which holds. Replacing the final datum by −4 gives cycle sum one and no global potential, although each individual edge equation has solutions. The three incidence rows have rank two, so two independent edge equations form a rank witness, but the third still supplies a consistency test on the right-hand side.","conclusion":"Local solvability, coefficient rank and right-hand-side consistency are distinct and explicitly measurable."}
limits: The result is a finite linear gluing theorem. It does not establish universal interoperability among proof systems or determine nonlinear obstruction classes without definitions and hypotheses.
extension: Replace scalar potentials by vectors or nonabelian group transports. Identify the appropriate cycle-holonomy obstruction, analyze gauge equivalence and determine which spanning-tree data plus residual loop checks form a complete certificate.

title: A prime-supported quadratic energy has an elementary constrained minimizer
revised_question: What does a quadratic energy over primes actually determine before asymptotic prime-density or zeta-zero corrections are invoked?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: A finite counting measure on primes gives an exact convex minimization problem. Its uniform minimizer and partition function depend only on the number of primes when every site has equal energy, so no fine prime-correlation information can appear in that model.
definitions_json: ["Let P_N={p prime:p≤N}, M=|P_N| and dπ_N=∑_{p∈P_N}δ_p. For real values a_p define F(a)=∑a_p².","Impose the affine constraint ∑a_p=A. Assume M≥1.","For constant site energy c², define Z_N(β)=∑_{p≤N}e^{−βc²}, with a finite fixed N."]
theorem_name: Uniform minimizer and degenerate partition statistics
theorem_statement: F(a)≥A²/M, with equality exactly at a_p=A/M for every prime. For constant energy, Z_N=M e^{−βc²}; mean energy is c² and energy variance is zero at every β.
theorem_proof: Cauchy–Schwarz gives (∑a_p)²≤M∑a_p², and its equality condition forces all coordinates equal. This proves the unique constrained minimizer; a Lagrange multiplier gives the same result through 2a_p=λ. For the partition function every summand is identical, giving the closed form. Then −∂_βlog Z=c² and ∂²_βlog Z=0. Thus fine spacings or correlations between prime labels cannot influence these statistics, because replacing P_N by any M-element set leaves the model unchanged. Likewise (cp)/(p/c)=c² cancels p whenever c and p are nonzero; prime support remains in the index set rather than in that individual value.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take N=10, whose primes are 2,3,5,7, and A=8.","calculation":"The minimizer is (2,2,2,2), with energy 16. The alternative (1,2,2,3) has the same sum but energy 18. For c=2, Z=4e^{−4β}; normalized probabilities are 1/4 each, independently of β, and the Shannon entropy is log4.","conclusion":"The finite measure and optimization are exact and show which information the model retains."}
limits: Approximating dπ by dx/log x is an asymptotic statement requiring an error theorem; it is not an equality of measures. Zeta-zero corrections matter only for a quantity that actually depends on prime positions.
extension: Introduce a stated position-dependent energy E(p) or coupling between primes, derive its finite partition derivatives, and use partial summation to identify exactly where a prime-counting remainder enters an asymptotic estimate.

title: Public depth recursions certify algebraic consistency, not sequential work
revised_question: What does the depth law c_{d+1}=c_d² prove, and what extra hypothesis is needed to certify an execution history?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: The double-exponential recurrence is solved exactly and linearized by a double logarithm. An elementary bad-event union bound explains a conditional composition claim, while showing that public endpoint consistency alone does not certify how an endpoint was computed.
definitions_json: ["Fix c₀>1 and integer d≥0, with c_{d+1}=c_d². Let a claimed trajectory contain both its endpoints and a declared local policy.","A verifier is algebraically sound with error α if an accepted false algebraic statement occurs with probability at most α under its defined experiment.","A second verifier is sound with error β for its own execution statement; a composed verifier accepts only when both accept."]
theorem_name: Closed form and conditional composition bound
theorem_statement: c_d=c₀^{2^d} and log log c_d=d log2+log log c₀. If every invalid composed claim implies failure of at least one of the two stated soundness properties, then its acceptance probability is at most α+β.
theorem_proof: Induction proves c_d=c₀^{2^d}; taking two logarithms gives the affine coordinate. For the probability statement let E₁,E₂ be the two bad-acceptance events. The hypothesis says invalid acceptance is contained in E₁∪E₂, so the union bound gives P≤P(E₁)+P(E₂)≤α+β, without assuming independence. The implication must actually be established for the composed statement; using a security parameter label does not establish it. The placeholder identity (c g)/(g/c)=c² is valid for nonzero g and c, but cancellation removes all dependence on g, including whether g is prime.

Also pitch octave equivalence is multiplication f↦2f; squaring f↦f² is not that same transformation unless an additional coordinate convention is chosen.","conclusion":"Endpoint arithmetic, depth coordinates, music analogies and execution claims are separately defined and checkable."}

title: Spectral flatness is an AM–GM statistic, not a false-acceptance exponent
revised_question: What does a spectral-flatness score prove, and what empirical evidence would support a tiny false-acceptance probability?

title: Changing the scalar domain changes solvability

status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: A linear Diophantine equation and a quadratic illustrate how the chosen scalar domain changes both existence and structure. The domains are connected by embeddings, but their divisibility, completeness and order properties cannot be interchanged.
definitions_json: ["Use N={1,2,…} and N₀={0,1,2,…}; this convention makes N⊂N₀⊂Z⊂Q⊂R⊂C.","For integers a,b not both zero, gcd(a,b) is their positive greatest common divisor. If x²=2 with x=r/s in lowest positive terms, r²=2s² makes r even; writing r=2k makes s even as well, contradicting coprimality. Completeness of R supplies √2, for example as the supremum of positive rationals with square below two. In an ordered field every square is nonnegative; therefore i²=−1 rules out an ordered-field structure on C extending ordinary arithmetic.

title: A power spectrum can fail to identify a finite sequence

theorem_statement: In Z/12Z the sets A={0,1,4,6} and B={0,1,3,7} have identical autocorrelation: value 4 at r=0, value 2 at r=6, and value 1 at every other nonzero r. They are not related by cyclic translation or reflection.

Enumerating the twelve ordered nonzero differences of each four-element set gives one occurrence at each residue 1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,10,11 and two at six. Hence all twelve spectral powers agree exactly. Translation preserves the cyclic gap multiset, as does reflection. The gaps of A are {1,2,3,6}, while those of B are {1,2,4,5}; the sets therefore cannot be related by either symmetry. This supplies a nontrivial collision beyond the familiar shift and reversal ambiguities.

title: Fibonacci transfer matrices give exact word growth and spectral data

summary: The same two-by-two matrix governs a substitution’s letter counts and a finite-state language’s path counts. Its eigenvalues give exact growth in both declared models, while a tight-binding transfer matrix is derived from a separate recurrence rather than identified with them by name.
