title: A secretless feature verifier factors through its observation fibers
revised_question: What exact hypothesis makes a decision rule depend only on a public feature map?
status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: A function factors through an observation map precisely when it is constant on every observation fiber. This elementary theorem yields a sharp impossibility statement for indistinguishable valid and invalid histories, without asserting that every possible public verifier must use the same features.
definitions_json: ["Let X be a set of histories, F:X→Y an observed feature map and V:X→{0,1} a deterministic verifier.","Write x∼x′ when F(x)=F(x′), and restrict Y to F(X) when constructing a factorization.","A randomized verifier based only on F has an acceptance probability v(F(x)); equal features then imply equal acceptance laws."]
theorem_name: Fiberwise factorization criterion
theorem_statement: There exists v:F(X)→{0,1} with V=v∘F if and only if V is constant on every fiber. If one fiber contains both a valid and an invalid history, no verifier based only on F can accept the former with probability at least 1−ε and the latter with probability at most ε for ε<1/2.
theorem_proof: Necessity follows by substitution: equal F values give equal v values. For sufficiency define v(y)=V(x) for any preimage x of y; fiberwise constancy proves independence of the choice. This is a set-theoretic factorization, requiring neither conical geometry nor secrecy. In the randomized case let the common acceptance probability be p. The two desired guarantees require p≥1−ε and p≤ε, impossible unless ε≥1/2. Consequently a lower bound requires construction of an actual mixed-validity fiber for the declared observation map, not merely a claim that the system has no secrets.

If the specification declares adjacent ones valid and separated ones invalid, the fiber contains opposite labels. A count-only verifier cannot distinguish them, whereas a verifier reading the full word can. Likewise the homometric Fourier patterns in the spectral example are indistinguishable to power-only features but distinguishable to their original sequences.","conclusion":"The limitation belongs to a precise observation algebra, rather than to all computation in a public system."}

title: Hash chains preserve order while holonomy uses a different algebra

status: Developed mathematical treatment with explicit hypotheses, derivation and checked example
summary: A nested hash update is order-sensitive rather than inherently abelian. Matrix transport gives a separate noncommutative loop invariant, and both constructions require declared equivalences and collision assumptions before they can certify histories.
definitions_json: ["A hash-chain update has h_{t+1}=H(h_t∥m_t), using unambiguous serialization. If the recorded path language allows an edge followed by its reverse, holonomy identifies that two-step record with the empty path; the hash map also has collisions on unrestricted histories.

Conversely (0,3) and (1,0) both end at three for this toy hash, illustrating collisions. Any fixed b-bit hash has only 2^b endpoints, so arbitrarily many finite histories force collisions by pigeonhole; computational collision resistance is a different property. Direct multiplication of U,V and their inverses proves the commutator formula. When backtracking is allowed as recorded history, UU⁻¹=I gives an explicit endpoint collision with the empty word; no such claim is made for the restricted positive-word monoid. Under a basepoint change of gauge G, a closed path product becomes GHG⁻¹, so its conjugacy class, rather than its raw matrix, is the natural gauge invariant.

title: Exponential connections produce periods without proving their independence

title: An elliptic curve has nontrivial self-extensions even for a stable line bundle

title: A heat-trace asymptotic is different from a trace-class statement at a fixed time
revised_question: Reconstruction: What exact example separates small-time divergence from trace class for every positive heat time?
status: Classical result or newly stipulated finite model; historical claims explicitly delimited
summary: The HED audit correctly separates asymptotic information about a spectral diagnostic from an operator-ideal assertion. A diagonal heat semigroup makes the distinction precise. It also supplies error bounds that can replace an unreachable absolute threshold.
definitions_json: ["On ℓ²(N₀), let A have diagonal eigenvalues n, n≥0. The heat operator H_t=e^{−tA} has eigenvalues e^{−tn}, t>0.","A positive diagonal operator is trace class exactly when its diagonal entries have a finite sum. Small-time heat behavior concerns t→0 rather than a fixed t."]

theorem_statement: H_t is trace class for every t>0, with TrH_t=1/(1−e^{−t})=t^{−1}+1/2+O(t) as t→0. Its trace diverges as t→0, and H_t converges strongly to the noncompact identity. The trace-norm truncation tail after n=N is e^{−t(N+1)}/(1−e^{−t}).

For a fixed vector x∈ℓ², ||(H_t−I)x||²=Σ_n|e^{−tn}−1|²|x_n|² tends to zero by dominated convergence, since the multiplier is bounded by one. Identity is not compact because the standard basis has no norm-convergent subsequence. Thus trace-class operators can converge strongly to a noncompact operator while their trace norms diverge. This does not contradict trace-norm closedness because convergence is only strong. For a trace difference, a cancellation of leading asymptotic coefficients likewise says nothing by itself about whether the corresponding operator difference is trace class at a fixed parameter.

Keeping indices n=0,…,9 gives trace 2−2^{−9}, and the exact positive tail is 2^{−9}=1/512. At t=log2/2 the trace is 1/(1−1/√2)=2+√2, showing sensitivity to the time scale without any failure of trace class.","conclusion":"The model gives separately a summability theorem, an asymptotic formula and an explicit numerical cutoff certificate."}

The remaining form pairs only q₁ and p₁, and its kernel within the three-dimensional level set is the one-dimensional translation direction. Because it is invariant and annihilates vertical vectors, it descends to the quotient; in the quotient coordinates its matrix is the standard invertible two-dimensional symplectic matrix. title: A Lyapunov metric certifies coercivity even when the Euclidean symmetric part fails

status: Classical result or newly stipulated finite model; historical claims explicitly delimited
summary: The Coercivity SDK source highlights a Jacobian with zero eigenvalues that cannot receive an unsupported strict certificate. A constructive positive example explains what a valid metric-based certificate looks like and why Euclidean eigenvalue checks alone are insufficient.
definitions_json: ["For x′=Ax with real A, take a symmetric positive-definite P and define ||x||_P²=xᵀPx. A certificate with rate α>0 is AᵀP+PA≼−2αP.","For a perturbation E define its P-operator norm ||E||_P=||P^{1/2}EP^{−1/2}||₂."]
theorem_name: A Lyapunov metric certifies coercivity even when the Euclidean symmetric part fails

For the perturbed generator, 2xᵀPEx is at most 2||x||_P||Ex||_P≤2δ||x||_P², giving the new rate. If Av=0 for a nonzero real or complex vector, the left quadratic form at v is zero while the strict right side is negative, a contradiction. More generally the same eigenvector calculation forces every eigenvalue to have real part at most −α. Conversely, a positive Euclidean symmetric part in some directions need not prevent stability, because a different metric may compensate for transient nonnormal growth.

Then tr(SX)=tr(RᵀSR), a sum of nonnegative diagonal quadratic forms. If the gap is zero, weak duality sandwiches every feasible primal value above the dual value and every feasible dual value below the primal one, so the pair is optimal. This argument requires only exact feasibility and positivity. summary: The source’s CU kernel uses prime-factor sets, approved-grounded factors and maximal-clique worlds. Define A⊢B when Pf(B)⊆Pf(A).","For required support R, repair the current support S by cl_R(S)=S∪R. In a compatibility graph, a clique is a set with every pair compatible; maximal means no further vertex can be added while retaining that property."]

A separate approved-grounded set G⊆S changes admissibility to R⊆G and may require evidential repair even when asserted support already contains R. For the graph limitation, take three Boolean constraints x=0, y=0 and x∨y=1. Every pair has a satisfying assignment, so the compatibility graph is a triangle and its full vertex set is a maximal clique. All three together are inconsistent. title: Authority composition is a meet calculation with an explicit proof dependency graph
revised_question: Reconstruction: What composition rule prevents a derived certificate from silently exceeding the authority of its premises?
status: Classical result or newly stipulated finite model; historical claims explicitly delimited
summary: The May artifact calculus proposed a six-coordinate authority profile. A precise finite poset model makes the intended monotonicity rule executable, while retaining the distinction between an order-theoretic accounting theorem and the truth of any mathematical assertion entered into the system.
definitions_json: ["Let A={0,1,2}⁶ with coordinatewise order and meet a∧b given by coordinatewise minimum. A dependency graph is a finite directed acyclic graph; every node has a local authority cap c(v).","For a source node set a(v)=c(v). At any later node define a(v)=c(v)∧∧_{u→v}a(u). theorem_name: Authority composition is a meet calculation with an explicit proof dependency graph
theorem_statement: For every node v, a(v) is the meet of c(w) over all ancestors w of v, including v. It is the largest profile simultaneously bounded by all those caps. Adding an additional dependency can only decrease or preserve the profile.
theorem_proof: Order the graph topologically. The claim is immediate for a source. If it holds for the predecessors of v, substituting their ancestor meets into the defining equation gives exactly the union of their ancestor sets together with v; repeated factors do not matter because meet is idempotent. This proves the formula by induction. Any other profile bounded by every ancestor cap is bounded by their meet, so the formula is the greatest admissible profile. Enlarging the ancestor set introduces further meet factors and cannot raise any coordinate. None of these steps supplies a proof that an individual premise is true: that requires a separately checked derivation. A soundness statement is conditional: if the local inference rules preserve truth and the source propositions are true, induction through the same graph proves every output proposition true.

title: A chain contraction proves homology equivalence and survives a controlled elementary perturbation
revised_question: Reconstruction: Which exact matrix identities certify a reduction of a chain complex, and what happens when a contractible coefficient changes?
status: Classical result or newly stipulated finite model; historical claims explicitly delimited
summary: The source lists chain complexes, maps, homotopies and contraction equations. We fix their signs and prove a complete reduction in a finite model. This supplies constructive homological content without treating artifact counts as homology calculations.
definitions_json: ["Use homological degree: d:C_k→C_{k−1}, d²=0. A reduction to H consists of chain maps i:H→C and p:C→H with pi=I and ip−I=dh+hd for a degree +1 map h.","Over Q let C₁=Qe and C₀=Qu⊕Qv, with d(e)=u, and let H₀=Qv, H_k=0 otherwise."]

In the example, on e the map hd is −I, while on u the map dh is −I and on v both sides vanish. Therefore ip−I=dh+hd in every degree. Changing the nonzero coefficient simply rescales the inverse on the contractible summand. The equation at ε=−1 is exceptional: d becomes zero, so both e and u become new homology classes and no reduction to the old one-dimensional H can exist. Formally 1/(1+ε)=Σ_{j≥0}(−ε)^j when |ε|<1; in a nilpotent filtered coefficient ring the same series terminates and gives an exact algebraic inverse. This elementary calculation exhibits the invertibility hypothesis behind homological perturbation rather than asserting a full perturbation lemma without its side conditions.

title: Finite-field construction needs an irreducible polynomial and an explicit generator image

status: Classical result or newly stipulated finite model; historical claims explicitly delimited
summary: The frontier followup lists finite-field witnesses and warns about generator maps and primitive tests. A complete field of eight elements gives constructive arithmetic and explains the important distinction between irreducible, primitive and embedded.
definitions_json: ["Let f(T)=T³+T+1 over F₂ and F=F₂[T]/(f), with α the residue of T. Represent every element uniquely by a binary polynomial of degree at most two.","Frobenius is x↦x². An embedding from a quotient F₂[U]/(g) must specify an element β satisfying g(β)=0, and then sends U to β."]

theorem_proof: A cubic over a field is reducible if and only if it has a linear factor. Here f(0)=f(1)=1, proving irreducibility and hence that the quotient is a field. Its nonzero multiplicative group has seven elements; α is neither zero nor one, and Lagrange implies its order is seven because seven is prime. Direct reduction with α³=α+1 also verifies α⁷=1. In any field of characteristic two, squaring respects sums and products, so Frobenius is a homomorphism. It is injective and hence surjective on a finite field. Every nonzero element has seventh power one, so x⁸=x for every element; thus the third iterate is identity. Applying Frobenius to f(α)=0 proves the conjugate equations. The three conjugates are distinct because α has order seven and the exponents1,2,4 differ modulo seven. An embedding is therefore a concrete substitution map, not merely an equality of field sizes.

A primitive-root test must actually exclude the identity element, especially when the group order is prime.","conclusion":"The example provides a full arithmetic table and explicit automorphism certificate."}

If two codewords were both within distance one of a received word, their mutual distance would be at most two by the triangle inequality, contradicting the minimum distance. A one-bit error has syndrome equal to its column, so the proposed decoder recovers its location and removes it. The balls have size eight, and16 codewords times eight equals128, the total number of binary seven-vectors, so these disjoint radius-one balls cover the space.

title: The cusp parametrization, local intersection and blowup are compatible exact calculations

Under y=tx the defining equation becomes t²x²−x³=x²(t²−x). The strict transform therefore has gradient(−1,2t), whose x-component is always−1, proving smoothness including over the exceptional point x=t=0. Its intersection with the exceptional divisor x=0 is t²=0, so the strict transform is smooth but tangent to that divisor; resolving the curve singularity and obtaining a normal-crossings total transform are different goals.

title: Species counting is an exact weighted partition problem with a convergent Euler product

status: Classical result or newly stipulated finite model; historical claims explicitly delimited
summary: The May asymptotic source supplies the decisive reduction to primorial logarithms. We prove the bijection, construct the partition function, and derive a rigorous upper bound. This gives useful exact mathematics before any saddle approximation is invoked.
definitions_json: ["For a species a₁≥a₂≥⋯≥0 of finite support set d_j=a_j−a_{j+1}≥0. Let P_j=∏_{i≤j}p_i and w_j=logP_j.","Define S(t)=#{d of finite support:Σ_jd_jw_j≤t}. For s>0 set Z(s)=∏_{j≥1}(1−e^{−sw_j})^{−1} and F(s)=logZ(s)."]

This proves the product identity and the bijection, since differences recover d uniquely. Also w_j≥jlog2, so Σ_je^{−sw_j} converges geometrically. For all sufficiently large j the terms are at most1/2, and −log(1−x)≤2x there; hence F(s) converges. Expanding each nonnegative geometric series gives Z(s)=Σ_dexp(−sΣd_jw_j), justified by monotone convergence. Every partition of weight at most t contributes at least e^{−st}; therefore S(t)e^{−st}≤Z(s), proving the bound. For a finite t only weights w_j≤t can occur, so S(t) can also be computed by a finite exact recursion using integer primorial products, avoiding logarithmic rounding.

title: An exponent species has a unique least integer representative

status: Classical result or newly stipulated finite model; historical claims explicitly delimited
summary: The SIT fragment specifies species (3,2,1), least representative360 and arithmetic invariants. We formulate the underlying optimization exactly and prove its general rearrangement rule. This is independent of whether the historical Lean tranche compiled.
definitions_json: ["A species is a finite nonincreasing list a₁≥⋯≥a_r≥1 of prime exponents. Its representatives are positive integers with that multiset of nonzero exponents. Let p_i denote the i-th prime.","Define the least candidate m(a)=∏_{i=1}^r p_i^{a_i}. Arithmetic invariants are Ω=Σa_i, ω=r and τ=∏(a_i+1)."]
theorem_name: An exponent species has a unique least integer representative
theorem_statement: m(a) is the unique least positive integer in its species. Its divisor-count, total-prime-factor and distinct-prime-factor invariants are exactly the stated product and sums.
theorem_proof: First any chosen r distinct primes q₁<⋯<q_r satisfy q_i≥p_i. Replacing them by the first r primes without changing exponent assignments cannot increase the product and strictly decreases it if any chosen prime differs. Next if p<q but exponents a<b are assigned in the wrong order, compare p^a q^b with p^b q^a: their ratio is (q/p)^{b−a}>1. Swapping the exponents strictly decreases the number. Repeated exchanges put the exponents in descending order on ascending primes. Equality permits only swaps among equal exponents, which do not change the integer, proving uniqueness of the numerical minimizer. Every divisor independently chooses an exponent between zero and a_i, yielding τ; counting factors with and without multiplicity gives Ω and ω.

Exhaustively assigning these exponents to the first few primes verifies the exchange proof’s finite predictions.","conclusion":"The least-representative theorem gives SIT a concrete arithmetic object and an exact comparison principle."}

summary: The July31 representation discussion includes rationals, reals and p-adics. A valuation makes this distinction precise: it changes which approximations are small, while preserving ordinary algebraic equalities on the embedded rational field. title: A cutoff theorem with the quantifiers made explicit
revised_question: When does increasing approximation resolution remain compatible with vanishing data noise, uniformly over a specified model class?
status: Proved under the stated hypotheses; newly stipulated examples
summary: The recovered master inequality becomes useful only after the model class, data norm and quantifiers are fixed. The fundamental issue is that approximation can improve while noise amplification becomes arbitrarily large. A diagonal parameter choice reconciles these two limits without requiring a guessed convergence rate.
definitions_json: ["Let A:X→Y be bounded between normed spaces, let M⊂X be a specified nonempty class, and let R_n:Y→X be bounded linear maps. Data satisfy yδ=Ax+e with ||e||≤δ.","Define B_M(n)=sup_{x∈M}||R_nAx−x||, S(n)=||R_n||, and Eδ(R_n;M)=sup_{x∈M,||e||≤δ}||R_n(Ax+e)−x||. Assume B_M(n) is finite and tends to zero."]

theorem_statement: Eδ(R_n;M)≤B_M(n)+δS(n). There exists an integer choice n(δ)→∞ with Eδ(R_{n(δ)};M)→0. Every choice with B_M(n(δ))→0 and δS(n(δ))→0 has this property.
theorem_proof: Add and subtract R_nAx and apply the triangle inequality and the operator norm bound. For existence choose a strictly increasing sequence n_j with B_M(n_j)≤1/j. Put s_j=max(1,S(n_1),…,S(n_j)), and choose strictly decreasing positive d_j→0 with d_j≤1/(j s_j). For d_{j+1}<δ≤d_j use n(δ)=n_j. Then δS(n(δ))≤1/j and the total bound is at most 2/j. As δ→0 the interval index j→∞, hence the result. This proof does not assume that S is monotone or that B has a power-law rate. Uniform convergence of B is a substantive hypothesis: pointwise convergence R_nAx→x for each fixed x does not imply it on an arbitrary unbounded class. If A has a nonzero kernel and M contains x and x+h with h∈ker A, a uniform error tending to zero is impossible, since the data coincide. Thus the model class must encode identifiable information as well as approximation smoothness.

title: Mild ill-posedness: an optimal rate from a concrete ellipsoid

status: Proved under the stated hypotheses; newly stipulated examples
summary: The source rate δ^{r/(p+r)} has a clean deterministic interpretation. It is the minimax order for a diagonal operator with polynomial singular values and a Sobolev-type ellipsoid. A two-point indistinguishability argument supplies the lower bound, so the rate expresses an information limitation rather than only the quality of one algorithm.

theorem_statement: For sufficiently small δ>0, spectral cutoff with N=⌊δ^(−1/(p+r))⌋ has worst-case error O(δ^{r/(p+r)}). No reconstruction map improves this order uniformly on M_r under norm-bounded noise.

The stated N balances the two terms and gives the upper order. For the lower bound put K=⌈δ^(−1/(p+r))⌉ and v=K^(−r)e_K. Both v and −v belong to M_r and ||Av||=K^(−(p+r))≤δ. The observation zero can thus arise from v with noise −Av or from −v with noise Av. For any output z=T(0), the triangle inequality gives max(||z−v||,||z+v||)≥||v||. Since K≤2δ^(−1/(p+r)) for δ≤1, this is at least 2^(−r)δ^{r/(p+r)}. This applies to every possible estimator. It also explains why stronger algorithms alone cannot remove the smoothness–noise tradeoff.

title: Tikhonov filters: qualification and explicit constants
revised_question: How do a spectral source condition and the filter maximum produce a complete Tikhonov error estimate?
status: Proved under the stated hypotheses; newly stipulated examples
summary: The filter formula in the recovered manuscript can be strengthened into an explicit theorem, including the range of smoothness for which the simple argument works. The parameter α controls both spectral bias and amplification; the source exponent determines their balance.
definitions_json: ["Let A:X→Y be bounded between Hilbert spaces and define R_α=(A* A+αI)^(−1)A*, α>0. Assume x†=(A* A)^νw, ||w||≤ρ, with 0<ν≤1.","The source condition places x† in ker(A) perpendicular and specifies spectral smoothness. Fractional powers are defined by the spectral calculus of the nonnegative bounded self-adjoint operator A* A."]

theorem_statement: For ||yδ−Ax†||≤δ, ||R_αyδ−x†||≤ρ cν α^ν+δ/(2√α), where cν=ν^ν(1−ν)^(1−ν) for0<ν<1 and c1=1. Forρ>0, a parameter of order (δ/ρ)^{2/(2ν+1)} gives error O(ρ^{1/(2ν+1)}δ^{2ν/(2ν+1)}).

Differentiating log(t^ν/(1+t)) gives ν/t−1/(1+t), so the maximum occurs at t=ν/(1−ν) when0<ν<1 and equals cν. Atν=1 the supremum is1. The noise multiplier is √λ/(λ+α); its derivative vanishes at λ=α and its global maximum is1/(2√α). The spectral theorem and the triangle inequality give the bound. Balancing α^νρ with δα^(−1/2) gives the parameter order and rate. The restriction ν≤1 is meaningful: forν>1 the ratio t^ν/(1+t) is unbounded on[0,∞), so this scale-free source estimate no longer follows from the same argument. A bounded spectrum gives another estimate, but it does not produce arbitrary qualification for ordinary Tikhonov regularization.

title: Landweber iteration: regularization by stopping
revised_question: How can an iterative algorithm converge for exact data yet need early stopping for noisy data?
status: Proved under the stated hypotheses; newly stipulated examples
summary: The recovered Landweber filter makes the role of iteration count precise. Increasing m shrinks the spectral residual and increases the noise norm. The same controlled-approximation principle used for spectral cutoff therefore governs an algorithm with no explicit truncation.
definitions_json: ["Let A be bounded between Hilbert spaces,0<ω≤||A||^(−2), and start x_0=0. Define x_{m+1}=x_m+ωA*(yδ−Ax_m). For A=0 the discussion is trivial, so assume ||A||>0.","Assume x†=(A*A)^νw withν>0 and||w||≤ρ. At singular valueσ>0, g_m(σ)=[1−(1−ωσ²)^m]/σ, while the residual on λ=σ² is(1−ωλ)^m."]

The maximum of λ^νexp(−ωmλ) overλ≥0 is(ν/(eωm))^ν, giving the bias estimate. For noise use1−(1−t)^m≤min(1,mt) on[0,1]. Thus |g_m(σ)|≤min(1/σ,mωσ)≤√(mω): below the crossing use the second term and above it use the first. The operator norm follows by spectral calculus. Balancing m^(−ν)ρ andδm^(1/2) gives the rate. revised_question: What can be established exactly about C0 without recovering the original front ODE or treating numerical agreement as its proof?

summary: The recovered integral is a well-defined mathematical object even though the governing front equation and normalization did not survive retrieval. status: Proved for the stated exact model; historical large-run claims remain unverified
summary: The recovered program names transformer gauge orbits and deployment-filtered symmetries. Several exact identities can be proved at module level. Their continuous algebraic freedom must not be confused with byte-exact quantized deployment, and nonlinear gates prevent an unrestricted hidden-basis change.
definitions_json: ["For column vectors q,k,v, an attention score without positional rotations is qᵀk; after RoPE it is qᵀR_δk with R_δ orthogonal. The value/output composition is Ov.","A SwiGLU block is D[SiLU(Gx)⊙Ux], where SiLU acts coordinatewise. A grouped-query pattern consists of g key/value groups, each shared by r query heads. All identities below require consistent changes of corresponding weights and biases."]
theorem_name: Exact module gauges and structural permutation group
theorem_statement: For invertible A and B, q→Aq,k→A⁻ᵀk preserves unrotated scores, and v→Bv,O→OB⁻¹ preserves outputs. RoPE scores are preserved if Aᵀ commutes with every R_δ. SwiGLU allows a common hidden permutation and arbitrary nonzero diagonal rescaling of its linear U branch, compensated in D. Permutations preserving g equal sharing groups form S_r wr S_g=(S_r)^g⋊S_g.
theorem_proof: The score identity is qᵀAᵀA⁻ᵀk=qᵀk, while the rotated score becomes qᵀAᵀR_δA⁻ᵀk and therefore needs the commutation condition. In one genuine two-dimensional rotation plane with sinδ≠0, solve CR=RC entrywise: the commutant is C=aI+bJ, J=[[0,−1],[1,0]], invertible when a²+b²≠0. Degenerate or repeated frequencies enlarge the commutant and must be treated separately. For values, (OB⁻¹)(Bv)=Ov. A hidden permutation P commutes with coordinatewise SiLU and respects the product: (Pa)⊙(Pb)=P(a⊙b). Scaling only the linear U branch by diagonal Λ scales the hidden product by Λ, canceled by D→DΛ⁻¹; scaling the nonlinear gate arbitrarily is invalid because SiLU is not homogeneous. A sharing-preserving permutation first permutes the g groups, then independently permutes their r query labels, proving the wreath-product decomposition. Arbitrary independent QK gauges across heads sharing one K generally break the sharing constraint.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take A=2I on one rotation plane, B=diag(2,3), and a two-channel SwiGLU with Λ=diag(2,−1). For g=r=2, count the sharing-preserving permutations.","calculation":"QK scores and VO products are unchanged by exact multiplication. The SwiGLU linear branch scaling is canceled by output columns, including the negative second factor. The structural permutation group has (2!)²·2!=8 elements, versus4!=24 unrestricted head permutations.","conclusion":"The model gives exact identities and a precise reason that an architecture-preserving gauge group is smaller than all coordinate transformations."}
limits: These identities do not certify any source Q4NX byte symmetry, finite-orbit optimum, runtime gain or generic completeness of the automorphism group. Quantization and residual normalization can reduce the admissible subgroup further.
extension: For the actual architecture and byte format, intersect the proved semantic gauge with all deployment predicates and construct exact certificates for each retained transformation.

title: Bellman-safe merging compares complete continuation behavior, not one current optimum
revised_question: Which state equivalence preserves every remaining decision, and in which direction does partition refinement move?
status: Proved for the stated exact model; historical large-run claims remain unverified
summary: The source reports Bellman quotient sequences such as8→6→3→2→1. Counts alone do not show that a quotient is valid. A finite-horizon recursion gives an exact sufficient equivalence, identifies the needed state information and explains when partition counts can legitimately decrease.
definitions_json: ["At time t, a state s has a finite legal action set A_t(s), immediate costs c_t(s,a), deterministic successor T_t(s,a), and terminal cost h at time L. Infeasible continuations have cost+∞.","Define equivalence backward: terminal states are equivalent when h agrees; at time t, states are equivalent when they have identical action labels and, for each action, identical immediate cost and equivalent successors. Keep the minimum accumulated prefix cost for each class."]
theorem_name: Continuation-preserving quotient theorem
theorem_statement: Equivalent states have equal cost for every legal labeled continuation and equal Bellman value. Replacing them by their class and retaining the cheapest prefix preserves the global optimum. On one fixed state set, a refinement splits classes and cannot lower their number.
theorem_proof: At the terminal stage, continuation cost is the agreed terminal value. Assuming the assertion at t+1, matching action labels, costs and successor classes gives matching cost for an action followed by any tail. Induction proves the full continuation statement and hence equality of its minimum. Two equivalent prefixes differ only in accumulated cost, so every future suffix adds the same amount; discarding the more expensive prefix cannot remove an optimum. For the partition direction, P refines Q precisely when every P-block lies within a Q-block; the induced map from P-blocks onto Q-blocks is surjective, so |P|≥|Q|. A decreasing numerical sequence may instead reflect backward horizons, elimination of unreachable states or deliberate validated merging; its direction is not evidence of a refinement theorem.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"At the final decision use states a,b,c with two actions L,R and cost vectors a=(0,10), b=(10,0), c=(0,10). All successors have zero terminal cost.","calculation":"a and c are equivalent and can merge. State b also has minimum value zero but is not continuation-equivalent: restricting the future to actionL yields cost0 froma and10 fromb. Thus equal scalar Bellman values are insufficient for a quotient required to survive changes in the allowed continuation set.","conclusion":"The quotient has a constructive correctness invariant rather than only an attractive reduction count."}
limits: This is a sufficient recursive bisimulation, not a claim that all possible weighted equivalences require identical immediate costs; potential reweighting can yield other exact quotient notions. The source’s actual state graphs were not recovered.
extension: Publish each state signature, successor map and class witness, then verify that every merge respects the declared continuation semantics and prefix-cost convention.

title: Channel erasure has exactly256 states only when forgotten lane identities are irrelevant
revised_question: Which exact physical-assignment model supports P(16,4)=43,680→4⁴=256 and a341-node route diagram bound?
status: Proved for the stated exact model; historical large-run claims remain unverified
summary: The source reports a dramatic channel-erasure quotient. A simple capacity model reproduces the counts and, more importantly, states the condition that makes erasure exact. The count itself does not validate a cost model or a route implementation.
definitions_json: ["Partition sixteen distinct channels into four banks of four lanes. Assign four labeled active objects injectively to physical channels. Erase the lane identity and retain only each object’s bank label.","Assume costs, all legal future choices and all required constraints depend only on bank labels and occupancy, and that no forgotten channel identity is pinned or externally observed. Each bank has capacity four."]
theorem_name: Exact quotient and diagram size
theorem_statement: There are16·15·14·13=43,680 physical assignments, and every one of4⁴=256 bank tuples is feasible. A tuple with bank occupancies n₁,…,n₄ has fiber size∏_bP(4,n_b). Under the stated invariance, minimizing cost over physical assignments is equivalent to minimizing over bank tuples. The full four-ary depth-four prefix tree has341 nodes.
theorem_proof: Injection counting gives the physical total. Any four-object bank tuple uses at most four objects in a bank, so its occupants can be assigned distinct lanes; this proves surjectivity of erasure. In each bank, its n_b labeled objects have P(4,n_b) injections into four lanes, and independent banks multiply the choices. If feasibility and cost are constant on each fiber, every physical feasible assignment projects to a quotient state of the same cost and every quotient state has a physical lift; the two infima therefore coincide. If future constraints distinguish two lanes, these hypotheses fail and the quotient must retain that information. The prefix count is1+4+4²+4³+4⁴=(4⁵−1)/3=341. Merging identical suffixes can reduce this diagram, but the tree bound already holds without claiming such merging.

Summing all256 fiber sizes gives43,680 exactly. Unequal fiber sizes show that the quotient is not automatically a uniform probability model.","conclusion":"Both reduction counts and the precise lift condition are established in a reproducible finite model."}
limits: The original routed graph, machine capacities, byte-hop objective and claimed9,765,632 optimum were not recovered. No timing or hardware claim is certified.
extension: Attach a lifting algorithm to every quotient transition and prove that capacity, lifetime and future-use constraints depend only on retained state; refine the state wherever this fails.

title: A frontier state supports exact min-plus transfer when it separates past from future
revised_question: What separator invariant makes frontier optimization exact, and when does a repeated-layer recurrence follow?
status: Proved for the stated exact model; historical large-run claims remain unverified
summary: The source combines fixed-height frontier DP, route occupancy and repeated min-plus transfer. A frontier is mathematically sufficient only when all interaction between processed and unprocessed choices passes through its retained state. A small transfer matrix proves an additive period law exactly.
definitions_json: ["Consider a finite constraint-and-cost problem with variables processed in a fixed order, each with at most D values. At a cut retain all assigned variables that occur in a factor involving an unassigned variable, together with any extra resource/connectivity state used by future factors.","Assume the retained boundary has at most κ variables and all forgotten factors have already been checked and charged exactly once. For a repeated layer let M_ij be the least additional cost of moving from boundary statei to statej, or+∞ if impossible."]
theorem_name: Exact separator recursion and repeated-layer transfer
theorem_statement: For each frontier signature, keeping the minimum accumulated cost preserves the global optimum. There are at most D^κ assignments before auxiliary states. Repeated identical layers satisfy v_(L+1)=v_L⊗M, where (v⊗M)_j=min_i(v_i+M_ij); hence v_L=v₀⊗M^⊗L.
theorem_proof: Any future factor sees the processed region only through the retained variables and resources. Two partial assignments with the same signature therefore admit exactly the same continuations and add the same future costs. Keeping their cheaper prefix is valid by direct substitution, and induction over the processing order proves the recursion. The D^κ bound counts boundary assignments, not extra partitions or capacities. For repeated layers, concatenate an optimal prefix to each one-layer transition and minimize the intermediate boundary state; this is precisely min-plus multiplication. Associativity follows because both bracketings minimize the same sum over all intermediate indices. An eventual period law is additional structure, not a consequence of observing several values.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Use two boundary states and M=[[+∞,2],[3,+∞]], with v₀=(0,+∞).","calculation":"M^⊗2=[[5,+∞],[+∞,5]], so M^⊗(L+2)=5+M^⊗L for every L≥0. The minimum terminal cost sequence is d₀=0,d₁=2,d₂=5,d₃=7,d₄=10, and d_(L+2)=d_L+5 exactly. This law follows from an exact matrix identity rather than fitting a short sequence.","conclusion":"The model supplies a concrete proof of both frontier compression and a repeated-layer recurrence."}
limits: The source’s lifetime-aware separator values, placement counts and recurrence constants require its actual graph and transition matrix. Auxiliary connectivity can dominate the bare D^κ bound.
extension: Publish the frontier extraction and transfer matrix, prove every future interaction crosses its signature and certify any claimed periodic law by min-plus matrix powers or a complete critical-cycle theorem.

title: Connectivity compression4140→128 is an exact rank theorem over the field with two elements
revised_question: Why can weighted partitions of an eight-vertex boundary admit128 representatives, and what completion criterion is preserved?
status: Proved for the stated exact model; historical large-run claims remain unverified
summary: The source reports connectivity compression from4,140 to128. These are not arbitrary empirical counts:4,140 is the eighth Bell number and128 is the exact rank of a standard connectivity matrix over F₂. A greedy weighted row basis preserves the best cost for every connected completion.
definitions_json: ["Let Π_k be all set partitions of a k-element boundary. Write p∨q for the least common coarsening and define M_pq=1 when p∨q has one block, zero otherwise, over F₂.","A cut is a two-coloring with vertex one fixed to colorzero; there are2^(k−1) cuts. Define C_p,c=1 when every block ofp is monochromatic under cutc. A weighted family assigns a finite costw(p) to each available partition."]
theorem_name: Exact connectivity rank and weighted representatives
theorem_statement: M=CCᵀ over F₂ and rank M=2^(k−1). Processing available C-rows in nondecreasing cost and retaining only linearly independent rows yields at most2^(k−1) representatives, preserving min{w(p):p∨q is one block} for every completionq.
theorem_proof: A cut constant on blocks of bothp andq is constant on each block ofp∨q. If that join hasb blocks, exactly2^(b−1) cuts qualify, odd exactly when b=1. Thus CCᵀ=M over F₂. The one-block partition has C-row equal to the trivial-cut unit vector. Each nontrivial bipartition has row equal to that unit vector plus its own cut unit vector. These rows span all2^(k−1) cut columns, so C has full column rank. Consequently Cᵀ is onto and C is injective, giving rank(CCᵀ)=2^(k−1). For weighted preservation, a discarded row is an F₂-sum of retained rows of no greater weight. If it is compatible withq, pairing that sum withC_q gives one; at least one retained row is also compatible and no more expensive. The reverse inequality follows because representatives are a subfamily. This proves equality of optimal completion costs.

The cut rank is2⁷=128. For k=3 there are five partitions and four cuts; exact F₂ elimination gives rankfour, and the weighted representative claim can be checked against all five completions.","conclusion":"The reduction has an exact algebraic certificate and a precisely stated weighted guarantee."}

title: Polynomial nullspaces expose minimal indices of singular pencils
revised_question: What can bounded-degree nullities actually prove about a singular pencil?
status: Developed classical mathematics with explicit hypotheses and scoped evidence
summary: The retrieved descriptor campaign reports left- and right-index-one controls through degree five. A complete exact toy pencil explains the nullity sequence and its finite-difference interpretation, while keeping bounded searches distinct from an unqualified completeness claim.
definitions_json: ["For a polynomial matrix F(λ), letν_d be the dimension over k of polynomial vectors v(λ) of degree at most d satisfyingFv=0; setν_{−1}=0. A minimal polynomial basis has right minimal indices ε₁,…,ε_s."]
theorem_name: Nullity growth certificate
theorem_statement: For a minimal polynomial basis, ν_d=Σ_i max(0,d−ε_i+1). Henceν_d−ν_{d−1} counts indices at most d, and its next difference counts indices exactly d. For F(λ)=[−λ,1], the only right minimal index is1 and there is no left polynomial nullspace.
theorem_proof: The displayed pencil equation is−λv₁+v₂=0, so every polynomial solution is h(λ)(1,λ). Its degree isdeg h+1 whenever h≠0, givingν₀=0 andν_d=d for d≥1. The generator has no common polynomial factor and cannot be replaced by a degree-zero nonzero vector, proving minimal index one directly. A left polynomial vector is a scalar h withh[−λ,1]=0, forcingh=0. In general a minimal basis has the predictable-degree property: polynomial combinations have degree governed by the largest coefficient-degree plus corresponding minimal index. Counting allowed polynomial coefficients gives the nullity formula. The direct calculation above needs no canonical-form algorithm. For a black-box finite-degree search, stabilization only proves absence of further indices when a suitable dimension or degree bound has also been established; an arbitrary stopping rule is not such a bound.

TransposingF exchanges the right-index-one example with a left-index-one example, giving the two reported control shapes without relying on floating eigenvalues.","conclusion":"Exact polynomial equations distinguish a singular-pencil structure from a regular pencil with infinite eigenvalues."}

title: Descriptor eigenvalue and damping sensitivities need a nonzero normalization
revised_question: How does a simple finite generalized eigenvalue move, and how does its damping ratio differentiate?
status: Developed classical mathematics with explicit hypotheses and scoped evidence
summary: The source reports descriptor intervention gradients and a numerical Fox–Kapoor agreement. The exact formula is derived here under the simple-eigenvalue hypothesis, with a fresh rational example. The reported benchmark and finite-difference residual are historical assertions rather than independently reproduced data.
definitions_json: ["Let A(t),E(t) be differentiable complex matrices, λ(t) a simple finite eigenvalue, Av=λEv and u* A=λu*E. Assumeu*Ev≠0. For λ=σ+iω≠0 defineζ=−σ/(σ²+ω²)^{1/2}."]
theorem_name: Generalized eigenvalue and damping derivative
theorem_statement: λ′=u*(A′−λE′)v/(u*Ev). Writingλ′=σ′+iω′ givesζ′=(−ω²σ′+σωω′)/(σ²+ω²)^{3/2}.
theorem_proof: DifferentiateAv=λEv: A′v+Av′=λ′Ev+λE′v+λEv′. Multiply byu*. The terms involvingv′ cancel becauseu*A=λu*E, leavingλ′u*Ev=u*(A′−λE′)v. The denominator assumption permits division and reveals the normalization sensitivity. Differentiatingζ=−σ(σ²+ω²)^{-1/2} and collecting terms gives the damping formula. Scaling either eigenvector cancels from the quotient, so no Euclidean normalization is required. At a multiple or defective eigenvalue a differentiable branch need not exist; atλ=0 the damping ratio itself is undefined. A finite-difference comparison is useful verification but does not remove either hypothesis or certify a finite intervention remainder. The example has right eigenvectorv=(1,−i)ᵀ and left rowu*=(1,i)/2, givingu*Ev=1. Substitution returns the same derivative without finite differencing. The general sensitivity is bounded by ||u||||v||·||A′−λE′||/|u*Ev|, so a small denominator signals sensitivity even if all entries are modest. At the defective family[[0,1],[t,0]], the eigenvalues±√t show why differentiability can fail at a collision.

title: A rotating residue has an exact period and a complete orbit decomposition
revised_question: Which state really advances by a fixed residue increment, and does its observed period equal the period of that full state?
status: Classical mathematics with newly authored derivation or explicitly defined worked model
summary: The recovered experiment used the formula p=k/gcd(k,r) for a buffer-related residue. That formula has a complete elementary proof once the state and update are stated. It certifies an orbit of a cyclic permutation; it does not, by itself, certify the period of every hidden state in a processor or execution.
definitions_json: ["Fix integers k≥1 and r. The state space is Z/kZ, and the update is F(x)=x+r modk. Let d=gcd(k,r), taking a nonnegative gcd.","A period is a positive integer p with F^p(x)=x. The least such integer is the orbit length. An observation h can identify different states, so h(F^n(x)) may have a shorter period."]
theorem_name: A rotating residue has an exact period and a complete orbit decomposition
theorem_statement: Every orbit of F has length p=k/d. There are exactly d orbits, each consisting of the residues in one congruence class modulo d. In particular, a genuine period two requires k even and r congruent to k/2 modulo k.
theorem_proof: Iteration gives F^n(x)=x+nr modk. Return to the initial state is equivalent to k dividing nr, independently of x. Write k=dk₀ and r=dr₀ with gcd(k₀,r₀)=1. Then k divides nr exactly when k₀ divides nr₀, which is equivalent to k₀ dividing n by coprimality. The least positive n is therefore k₀. Every increment is divisible by d, so an orbit remains in one class modulo d. That class has k/d elements, exactly the orbit length, proving equality and the d-orbit count. For length two, k/d=2 forces d=k/2 and hence r=(k/2) times an odd integer modulo k.

The remaining orbits are the other three congruence classes modulo four. The full residue has period three, but parity is constant along every one of these orbits, with observed period one. For a separate period-two case k=6,r=3, the orbit0→3→0 satisfies the theorem exactly. These integers illustrate the algebra; they are not asserted to be historical hardware parameters.","conclusion":"The period formula becomes an exact state-transition theorem, while the distinction between state period and observation period remains explicit."}

title: The linear perfect-power branch has an exact valuation formula and never becomes finite through underflow
revised_question: Which d-free coefficient controls the first hit and the counting constant?
status: Classical mathematics with newly authored derivation or explicitly defined worked model
summary: The classifier audit found an infinite branch misclassified after a floating coefficient underflowed. Conversely ca has every valuation divisible by d, so cn=(u t)^d with integer u=(ca)^(1/d). The bijection t↦at^d proves the count and infinitude. No approximate coefficient or limiting classification is required.

title: Irreducibility certificates do not by themselves classify rational points
revised_question: Which exact algebraic certificate can discharge an irreducibility task, and what additional theorem is needed before a curve classification follows?
status: Classical mathematics or a newly chosen finite model developed with proof; historical claims delimited
summary: The recovered October workload distinguishes curve modules, irreducible equations and point-carrying cases. These are different mathematical obligations. A reusable reduction certificate can settle a polynomial irreducibility statement, while point completeness still requires the actual arithmetic argument. The examples here are explicitly chosen models, not reconstructions of the unavailable positive-k equations.
definitions_json: ["A polynomial f in Z[x] is primitive when its coefficients have gcd one. Reduction modulo a prime p preserves its degree if p does not divide the leading coefficient.","Irreducibility is over a specified field. A rational-point completeness theorem asserts that every rational point satisfying the stated curve equation occurs in a specified list or parametrization."]
theorem_name: A sound finite-field route and its scope
theorem_statement: If a primitive f in Z[x] has degree-preserving irreducible reduction modulo p, then f is irreducible over Q. For degree two or three, irreducibility over F_p is equivalent to having no root in F_p. Neither statement supplies all rational points on an associated curve.
theorem_proof: Gauss’s lemma turns a nontrivial rational factorization into f=gh with primitive integer factors of positive degree. Because the leading coefficient of f is nonzero modulo p, both leading coefficients of g and h are nonzero modulo p. Reduction therefore preserves their positive degrees and contradicts irreducibility of the reduction. For a quadratic or cubic over a field, any nontrivial factorization has a linear factor, equivalent to a root; conversely a root gives a linear divisor. In higher degree, rootlessness alone is insufficient because both factors may have degree at least two. This proves a precise certificate rule with no appeal to numeric root approximations. The logical separation from point classification is visible already in a hyperelliptic equation y²=f(x): irreducibility of f does not determine which rational x make f(x) a square.

Its values at 0 and 1 are both 1, so it is an irreducible cubic and f is irreducible over Q. The curve y²=x³−x+1 has the easily checked rational points (0,±1), (1,±1) and (3,±5). Irreducibility alone neither produces these points nor proves that any proposed finite list is complete. For a sharper algebraic caution, x⁴+1 factors modulo three as (x²+x+2)(x²+2x+2), although it is irreducible over Q: after x↦x+1 it becomes x⁴+4x³+6x²+4x+2, which is Eisenstein at two. theorem_statement: For5≤n≤9 the minimum distance of C_n is exactlyn−4. Thus seven raw outputs correct one arbitrary word error, and nine correct two. No code representing all M states over this alphabet can correct one error with six words or two errors with eight words.
theorem_proof:
If two distinct state codewords agreed at five positions in any n≤9, the preceding theorem would make the states equal. They therefore agree in at most four positions, giving distance at leastn−4. Conversely, for any code of minimum distanced, puncturing d−1fixed positions leaves an injective map: otherwise two original words differed only in those positions, contradicting the distance. Hence its population is at mostb^{n−d+1}. Since M>b^4, one has n−d+1≥5, or d≤n−4. This proves equality.

Two Hamming balls of radius t are disjoint when the minimum distance exceeds2t, by the triangle inequality; hence the stated seven- and nine-word codes uniquely correct the stated errors. An explicit decoder enumerates five-position subsets, applies the certified affine-lattice decoder, re-encodes each candidate and retains a state within the permitted Hamming radius. Enough clean positions remain to produce the true candidate, and the distance proof rules out a second one. Finally any code correcting t arbitrary errors has distance at least2t+1. Puncturing2t positions must be injective, giving M≤b^{n−2t}; sinceM>b^4, necessarily n≥5+2t. This proves the requested length lower bounds without a linear-code assumption.

In its first nine words instead corrupt positions1 and7 by offsets54321 and98765 modulo b.","calculation":"The exact subset decoder returns the original state in both cases. The verification report retains all original and corrupted words. A word can be altered in many bits and still counts as one corruption in this model.","conclusion":"The finite decoder tests instantiate a globally proved distance theorem, and the puncturing bound proves that shorter full-population codes cannot have the same correction guarantee."}

title: Minimal recurrences connect observations to finite realizations
status: Classical framework with a proved synthesis and worked example
summary: A finite-state linear description and a recurrence for an observed sequence are two presentations of the same algebraic structure. The useful dimension is the reachable and observable dimension, which can be smaller than the dimension of the original matrix. This links the Cayley–Hamilton, observability, Fourier and exact-certificate questions without claiming that every nonlinear model has finite closure.
definitions_json: ["Work over a field F. A scalar sequence has a linear representation y_n=cAⁿb with finite-dimensional A, row c and column b. Its infinite Hankel matrix is H=(y_(i+j)) for i,j≥0.","The rank of the infinite Hankel matrix is the supremum of ranks of its finite submatrices. A recurrence of order r means y_(n+r)=Σ_(j=0)^(r−1)a_j y_(n+j) for every n≥0."]
theorem_name: Hankel rank equals the minimum linear realization dimension
theorem_statement: For a scalar sequence with a finite linear representation, the minimum possible state dimension equals rank H. It also equals the minimum order of an everywhere-valid forward recurrence, with the zero sequence assigned order zero.
theorem_proof: For any representation H factors as O R, where O has rows cAⁱ and R has columns Aʲb. Therefore rank H cannot exceed the state dimension. Restrict first to the reachable subspace span{Aʲb}, then quotient by its invisible subspace {v:cAⁱv=0 for all i}. The resulting representation is reachable and observable. In a minimal r-dimensional scalar realization, the first r Krylov columns are independent: the first linear dependence would make their earlier span A-invariant and stop further growth. The analogous statement holds for the first r observation rows. Their product is the leading r×r Hankel block, which is consequently invertible, proving rank H≥r. Cayley–Hamilton gives a recurrence of order at most r. Conversely, an order-r recurrence has an r-dimensional companion realization, so no smaller recurrence is possible. These arguments also account for finite transients, which can contribute nilpotent modes.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take y_n=2ⁿ+3ⁿ, generated by A=diag(2,3), b=(1,1)ᵀ and c=(1,1).","calculation":"The first values are 2,5,13,35,97. The leading 2×2 Hankel matrix is [[2,5],[5,13]], whose determinant is 1. The polynomial (z−2)(z−3)=z²−5z+6 gives y_(n+2)=5y_(n+1)−6y_n. Thus a two-state representation exists and the nonzero Hankel determinant rules out a one-state representation. If instead A=diag(2,−2), then y_n=2ⁿ+(−2)ⁿ has dimension two, while the even subsequence y_(2k)=2·4ᵏ has dimension one.","conclusion":"A short recurrence can be a certificate of exact observable compression. Subsampling can also erase modes, so reduced apparent dimension need not mean that the original dynamics became simpler."}
limits: Finite prefix agreement alone never proves an infinite recurrence without a model-class or order bound. Given any inspected prefix, a sequence that agrees there and changes later is indistinguishable on that prefix. Numerical Hankel rank additionally requires tolerances and perturbation analysis.
extension: Given an exact matrix family A(θ), determine where the reachable-observable dimension changes by computing rank minors. This is a finite algebraic question for a specified polynomial parameterization. For nonlinear polynomial dynamics, the degree-growth obstruction in M018 identifies an important class where a polynomial closure containing the state coordinate cannot be finite.

title: A reversible observation transform preserves Fisher information
status: Classical framework with a proved synthesis and worked example
summary: The Gudermannian can turn an unbounded coordinate into a bounded angle and simplify a formula. An exact reversible change of observation cannot itself create statistical information. This distinction turns the old activation and geometry questions into an analysis of representation, quantization, noise and numerical precision.
definitions_json: ["Let X have a regular density p_θ(x), with θ-independent support and square-integrable score s_θ=∂_θlog p_θ. Fisher information is I_X(θ)=E_θ[s_θs_θᵀ].","Let g be a θ-independent differentiable bijection with nonzero Jacobian on its domain. Y=g(X) is the same observation expressed in another coordinate."]
theorem_name: Fisher information is invariant under an invertible parameter-independent observation chart
theorem_statement: Under the stated change-of-variable and regularity assumptions, I_Y(θ)=I_X(θ). Additional quantization or a parameter-independent noisy channel cannot increase Fisher information when the score-conditioning identity and the usual differentiation conditions hold.
theorem_proof: The transformed density is q_θ(y)=p_θ(g⁻¹(y))|det Dg⁻¹(y)|. The Jacobian factor is independent of θ, so differentiating its logarithm with respect to θ gives zero. Consequently the transformed score is s_θ(g⁻¹(y)), and change of variables in its second moment proves equality. For a further observation Z produced through a θ-independent channel, differentiation under the integral gives s_Z(Z)=E[s_X(X)|Z]. Conditional Jensen yields E[s_Zs_Zᵀ]⪯E[s_Xs_Xᵀ], since their difference is E[Cov(s_X|Z)]. This is a statement about observations; reparameterizing θ has its own Jacobian transformation law and is a different operation.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Let X∼N(μ,σ²) with σ>0 known and take Y=gd(X)=arctan(sinh X), so −π/2<Y<π/2.","calculation":"The inverse is x=artanh(sin y), with dx/dy=sec y. Therefore q_μ(y)=exp(−(artanh(sin y)−μ)²/(2σ²))sec y/(σ√(2π)). Its μ-score is (artanh(sin y)−μ)/σ², and its squared expectation is 1/σ², exactly the original information. If Y is then rounded into a finite set of bins, the retained information becomes Σ_j (∂_μP_j)²/P_j and is at most 1/σ². The bundled calculation evaluates this finite-bin quantity directly from Gaussian CDFs.","conclusion":"The coordinate transformation is mathematically useful while its statistical information is unchanged. A benefit under a fixed finite-bit or hardware budget is possible, but it must be demonstrated for that budget and distribution."}
limits: The theorem does not forbid a transform from improving optimization behavior, finite-precision conditioning or a restricted approximation class. It also does not apply unchanged to a transform depending on an unknown θ. A bounded activation used inside a noninvertible network is not merely an observation chart.
extension: Compare candidate transforms at a fixed bit budget by optimizing retained information under a declared prior or worst-case parameter range. Include saturation, endpoint roundoff and added sensor noise. This yields a concrete design objective rather than a claim that bounded coordinates are intrinsically more informative.

title: Finite observations generate an algebra of distinguishable classes
status: Classical framework with a proved synthesis and worked example
summary: The common core of exact classification, graph signatures and probe selection is the partition induced by the available observations. On a finite state set, that partition has a complete algebraic description. This is stronger and more precise than assigning a complexity score to each state.
definitions_json: ["Let Ω be a finite set and f₁,…,f_m:Ω→R be exact observations, with m≥1. States x and y are equivalent when f_i(x)=f_i(y) for every i.","Let A be the unital algebra generated by the f_i under real linear combinations and pointwise products. Its elements are polynomial functions of the observation vector."]
theorem_name: The observation algebra is exactly the set of functions constant on observation classes
theorem_statement: If the observations induce K distinct classes, then A has dimension K and contains the indicator of each class. If every observation is invariant under a group action, no function in A can distinguish two states in the same orbit.
theorem_proof: Every polynomial in the observations is constant on each equivalence class, giving one inclusion. For the reverse inclusion choose a linear combination h=Σa_i f_i whose values h₁,…,h_K on the classes are all distinct. Such coefficients exist because equality on any two distinct observation vectors excludes only one proper hyperplane, and finitely many proper hyperplanes cannot cover R^m. The Lagrange polynomial ℓ_j(h)=∏_(k≠j)(h−h_k)/(h_j−h_k) is the indicator of class j. These K indicators span every function constant on the classes and are independent. This also gives a constructive integer choice: take a_i=T^(i−1). Each pairwise equality is a nonzero polynomial in T of degree at most m−1, so among more than (m−1)K(K−1)/2 distinct integers at least one choice avoids all equalities. Group invariance is preserved by sums and products, proving the orbit obstruction.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take Ω={(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)} and first observe f(x,y)=x+y.","calculation":"The observed values 0,1,1,2 give K=3 classes. Swapping coordinates preserves f, so no polynomial in f can separate (1,0) from (0,1). Add g(x,y)=x. The combined observation separates all four states; h=f+2g takes values 0,3,1,4. Its four Lagrange polynomials recover the four individual state indicators exactly. The verification script checks the indicator table using rational arithmetic.","conclusion":"An ambiguity caused by the observation partition cannot be repaired by increasingly elaborate postprocessing of the same data. A new probe must split the ambiguous class."}
limits: The finite-set hypothesis is essential to this elementary algebraic completeness statement. Exact equality, noisy equality and approximate separability are different questions. A coordinate identity or formal feature space may include states that no physical object realizes.
extension: For a specified family of admissible probes, define each probe’s covered pairs as those it separates. Minimum-cost separation of a finite target set becomes a weighted set-cover problem on state pairs. The certificate is exact only for that declared target population; it makes no automatic claim about unseen states or faults.

title: Heat observations separate exact recovery from stable recovery
status: Classical framework with a proved synthesis and worked example
summary: The heat-kernel questions contain two distinct issues. A compressed signature can lose information exactly, whereas the full kernel can be complete but poorly conditioned for reconstruction. The exact collision in M020 and the bounds below make both statements concrete.
definitions_json: ["Let L and M be real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices. At t>0 define K_L(t)=exp(−tL). Matrix norms below are Euclidean operator norms.","For a labeled undirected weighted graph, L is its combinatorial Laplacian. A heat trace, the diagonal of the heat kernel and the full heat kernel are different observations."]
theorem_name: Forward heat evolution is Lipschitz while its logarithmic inverse can amplify noise
theorem_statement: For t≥0, ||exp(−tL)−exp(−tM)||≤t||L−M||. For t>0, the full positive-definite kernel determines L uniquely by L=−log(K_L(t))/t. If t>0 and ||L||,||M||≤Λ, then ||L−M||≤e^(tΛ)||K_L(t)−K_M(t)||/t.
theorem_proof: Differentiate F(s)=exp(−(t−s)L)exp(−sM) with respect to s. Since F(t)−F(0)=exp(−tM)−exp(−tL), integration gives exp(−tL)−exp(−tM)=∫₀ᵗexp(−(t−s)L)(M−L)exp(−sM)ds. Each exponential has norm at most one because the generators are positive semidefinite; integrating norms proves the first bound. For positive-definite A and B with eigenvalues at least a>0, the resolvent integral for the logarithm and the identity U⁻¹−V⁻¹=U⁻¹(V−U)V⁻¹ give ||log A−log B||≤||A−B||∫₀∞(a+s)⁻²ds=||A−B||/a. The spectral lower bound for either heat matrix is e^(−tΛ); substitute a and divide by t. The principal logarithm is unique for a positive-definite matrix, which proves exact completeness of the full labeled kernel.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"The 4×4 rook graph and the Shrikhande graph have the same Laplacian spectrum 0,4 with multiplicity 6, and 8 with multiplicity 9, but different clique numbers.","calculation":"Both are vertex-transitive, so every diagonal heat value equals (1+6e^(−4t)+9e^(−8t))/16 for every t. Thus even all-time vertex heat signatures cannot distinguish these two graphs. Their full heat matrices do differ up to graph isomorphism, because equality after a vertex relabeling would force equality of their recovered Laplacians. For the full-kernel inverse bound, e^(tΛ)/t is minimized at t=1/Λ when Λ>0 and the absolute kernel-error budget is held fixed.","conclusion":"There can be exact blindness in a compressed signature and severe numerical sensitivity in a complete observation. Completeness and robustness must be evaluated separately."}
limits: The inverse bound applies to exact heat kernels of symmetric positive semidefinite generators with a common norm bound. An arbitrary noisy matrix need not remain positive definite; reconstructing a nearest valid generator is a separate constrained problem. The time 1/Λ minimizes this particular upper bound, not every practical estimator’s risk.
extension: Combine the exact observation partition with perturbation bounds: first determine which states are distinguishable in principle, then select times and probes that provide a specified margin under the declared noise model. This avoids optimizing a highly precise score on a fundamentally incomplete signature.

title: Positivity conservation entropy and spectra share one graph update
status: Classical framework with a proved synthesis and worked example
summary: A reaction–diffusion discretization becomes much more informative when its algebraic and probabilistic properties are checked together. For a finite undirected graph, one elementary step provides mass conservation, positivity, an entropy inequality and an explicit stability boundary.
definitions_json: ["Let a_ij=a_ji≥0, a_ii=0 define a connected finite weighted graph, with degrees d_i=Σ_j a_ij and d_max>0. Let L=diag(d)−A and P_h=I−hL.","For row probability vectors p, the update is p↦pP_h. The uniform distribution u is stationary whenever P_h is doubly stochastic."]
theorem_name: An explicit step is a Markov update precisely within its positivity range
theorem_statement: For 0≤h≤1/d_max, P_h is nonnegative and doubly stochastic, so it conserves probability and cannot decrease Shannon entropy. At h≤1/(2d_max), all eigenvalues of P_h are nonnegative. For h>0 in that latter range, every zero-sum vector contracts in Euclidean norm by at most 1−hλ₂(L), where λ₂ is the spectral gap.
theorem_proof: Off-diagonal entries of P_h are h a_ij≥0, diagonal entries are 1−h d_i and each row sums to one. Symmetry gives column sums one. With φ(s)=s log s and φ(0)=0, Jensen applied to each column gives φ((pP)_j)≤Σ_i P_ij φ(p_i); summing and using row sums proves Σφ(pP)≤Σφ(p), which is the entropy statement. Symmetric diagonalization gives eigenvalues 1−hλ_i(L). The bound λ_max(L)≤2d_max follows from xᵀLx=Σ_(i<j)a_ij(x_i−x_j)²≤2Σ_i d_i x_i². Therefore h≤1/(2d_max) makes all update eigenvalues nonnegative. On the orthogonal complement of constants, the largest is 1−hλ₂. Squaring gives the corresponding residual-energy contraction.
worked_example_json: {"setup":"For a periodic one-dimensional grid with diffusion coefficient D and mesh size Δx, the nearest-neighbor generator has degree 2D/Δx².","calculation":"The condition h≤1/d_max becomes r=DΔt/Δx²≤1/2, the usual positivity condition for the explicit stencil. Taking r≤1/4 also makes every Fourier multiplier nonnegative. At the endpoint r=1/2 on an even cycle, the alternating mode has multiplier −1 and does not decay: positivity and conservation hold, but convergence to equilibrium can fail through periodicity. A two-state swap gives the simplest example: p=(1,0) alternates with (0,1), preserving zero Shannon entropy.","conclusion":"A valid nonnegative conservative update need not be a strictly mixing update. The spectral calculation identifies the missing hypothesis and quantifies convergence once it is supplied."}
limits: Reaction terms, directed edges, nonuniform stationary measures and adaptive time steps need additional analysis. Entropy monotonicity for the uniform measure does not automatically transfer to arbitrary dynamics; a relative entropy against the correct stationary measure is often the relevant quantity.
extension: Design a discretization or graph update to satisfy a joint contract: mass, positivity, symmetry, entropy and a specified decay rate. Then verify each property algebraically before measuring prediction performance.

title: Whitening turns sensor questions into projection geometry
status: Classical framework with a proved synthesis and worked example
summary: The squared-residual, covariance and observation questions admit an exact common model for Gaussian mean changes. In this model one can calculate precisely what a linear sensor panel preserves and what it loses. The same calculation gives a robust margin and an impossibility statement for universal dimension reduction.
definitions_json: ["Let X∼N(μ+δ,Σ), where the baseline μ and positive-definite covariance Σ are known and δ is an unknown mean shift. Let B be a k×d matrix of full row rank and observe Y=BX.","Whiten the shift as d₀=Σ^(−1/2)δ. Define C=BΣ^(1/2) and the orthogonal projection P=Cᵀ(CCᵀ)⁻¹C onto the row space of C."]
theorem_name: A linear panel retains exactly the projected noncentrality
theorem_statement: The statistic T_B=(Y−Bμ)ᵀ(BΣBᵀ)⁻¹(Y−Bμ) has a noncentral χ²_k law with noncentrality λ_B=||P d₀||². Full observation has λ_full=||d₀||². Hence λ_B≤λ_full, with equality exactly when d₀ lies in the retained row space. If k<d, some nonzero shifts have λ_B=0.
theorem_proof: Write X−μ=Σ^(1/2)(Z+d₀) with Z standard normal. Multiplying by (CCᵀ)^(−1/2)C gives a k×d matrix with orthonormal rows. It maps Z to a standard k-dimensional normal, while the squared norm of the transformed shift is d₀ᵀCᵀ(CCᵀ)⁻¹Cd₀=||P d₀||². This proves the distribution and noncentrality formula. The Pythagorean identity ||d₀||²=||P d₀||²+||(I−P)d₀||² proves the inequality and equality condition. If k<d, the projection has a nontrivial kernel, giving a nonzero invisible shift. For perturbations d=d₀+e with ||e||≤ε, triangle inequality gives ||Pd||≥max(||Pd₀||−ε,0). Equality is attained by choosing e opposite to Pd₀ within the retained subspace, or by cancelling it completely when ε is large enough. Thus the exact worst-case noncentrality is max(||Pd₀||−ε,0)².
worked_example_json: {"setup":"Take Σ=I₃ and let B retain the first two coordinates. Then P=diag(1,1,0).","calculation":"A shift δ=(3,4,0) has λ_full=λ_B=25. A shift δ=(0,0,5) also has λ_full=25 but λ_B=0: the selected panel sees the null distribution exactly. For the first shift with whitened uncertainty radius ε=2, the worst-case retained noncentrality is (5−2)²=9, attained by perturbation e=(−6/5,−8/5,0). Under the null, T_B∼χ²₂, with mean 2 and variance 4; the full statistic has three degrees of freedom. Comparing only raw residual scores without this calibration can be misleading.","conclusion":"Exact optimization for a declared finite list of shifts is useful and checkable. Preserving every possible shift while reducing dimension is impossible in this model. Robustness can be expressed as a proved geometric margin rather than a hope that selected probes generalize."}
limits: Known Gaussian covariance, mean-shift alternatives and linear measurements are strong assumptions. Estimated baselines change calibration, non-Gaussian tails can invalidate χ² laws and nonlinear features need their own analysis. The noncentrality comparison alone is not a universal theorem about every detector at every significance level.
extension: For a finite target family {d_j}, choose a minimum-cost panel subject to max(||P_B d_j||−ε_j,0)²≥τ_j. Solve a small instance exactly and report every target and uncertainty set. This produces a concrete experimental-design certificate whose scope is visible.

title: Exact finite polynomial closure for triangular maps and its resonance strata
status: A complete theorem for the specified triangular family with exact examples; no novelty claim
summary: The univariate degree-growth obstruction in M018 has a substantial positive counterpart. Every triangular polynomial map T(x,y)=(ax,by+p(x)) admits an exact finite linear feature representation containing the original coordinate functions. Its smallest such space can be classified completely by collisions among the eigenvalues a^k. Repeated nonlinear eigenvalues reduce the required feature count, while resonances with b determine the only possible nontrivial Jordan chain. The same calculation yields an exact iterate formula and a criterion for removing the forcing by a polynomial fiber translation. An invertible coupled counterexample demonstrates why this is a theorem about a specified family, not a universal finite-closure principle.
definitions_json: ["Work over F=R or C with the polynomial ring F[x,y]. Let a,b∈F and p(x)=Σ_(k=0)^d c_kx^k, with zero coefficients omitted from its support. The Koopman operator is U_Tf=f∘T.","A feature space is an F-linear subspace W of polynomials with U_TW⊂W. It is not required to be closed under pointwise products. A finite-dimensional algebra containing x would already be impossible because it would contain every x^n.","Require W to contain 1,x,y. Let q(x)=Σ_(k≥2)c_kx^k, S={k≥2:c_k≠0}, Λ={a^k:k∈S}, and v_λ(x)=Σ_(k∈S,a^k=λ)c_kx^k for λ∈Λ.","On the diagonal subspace E=span{1,x,v_λ:λ∈Λ}, group all terms of p by their eigenvalue: p_μ(x)=Σ_(k≥0,a^k=μ)c_kx^k. For k=0 use a^0=1, including a=0. Missing groups mean the zero polynomial."]
theorem_name: Minimal feature dimension, resonance normal form and exact iterates
theorem_statement:
The unique smallest invariant linear feature space containing 1,x,y is W_min=span{1,x,y,v_λ:λ∈Λ}, and dim W_min=3+|Λ|. Its action is U1=1, Ux=ax, Uv_λ=λv_λ and Uy=by+p. Put z=y+Σ_(μ≠b)p_μ/(b−μ). Then Uz=bz+p_b and Up_b=bp_b. Consequently U|W_min is diagonalizable exactly when p_b=0; if p_b≠0 it has precisely one size-two Jordan block at b, with every other block of size one. Writing D={1,a,b}∪Λ as a set, its minimal polynomial is ∏_(μ∈D)(t−μ), multiplied by one further factor (t−b) when p_b≠0. Its characteristic polynomial, with multiplicities retained, is (t−1)(t−a)(t−b)∏_(λ∈Λ)(t−λ).

For n≥0 the exact state iterate is x_n=a^n x and y_n=b^n y+Σ_μ C_n(b,μ)p_μ(x), where C_0=0 and C_n(b,μ)=Σ_(j=0)^(n−1)b^(n−1−j)μ^j. For b≠μ this is (b^n−μ^n)/(b−μ); for b=μ≠0 it is n b^(n−1). The convolution sum is the definition at b=μ=0 and removes any 0^0 ambiguity: C_1=1 and C_n=0 for n≥2.
theorem_proof:
The proposed space is invariant because each v_λ is a polynomial eigenfunction, while Uy=by+c_0+c_1x+Σv_λ belongs to it. Every invariant W containing 1,x,y must contain q=Uy−by−c_0−c_1x and hence U^jq for every j. The distinct-eigenvalue decomposition is U^jq=Σ_(λ∈Λ)λ^jv_λ. Its first |Λ| rows form a Vandermonde matrix with nonzero determinant, including when one eigenvalue is zero. Therefore W contains each v_λ. Equivalently, applying the Lagrange spectral projector ∏_(ν≠λ)(U−νI)/(λ−ν) to q extracts v_λ. This proves minimality. The nonlinear group polynomials have disjoint nonempty monomial supports of degree at least two, so they are mutually independent and independent of 1,x,y. Thus the dimension formula follows even if a nonlinear eigenvalue coincides with 1 or a; that coincidence does not permit discarding the nonlinear vector.

The restriction to E is diagonal in the displayed basis, though its eigenvalues may repeat. Decompose p into its E-eigencomponents p_μ. Direct calculation gives U(y+h)−b(y+h)=p+(U−b)h. Taking h=Σ_(μ≠b)p_μ/(b−μ) cancels every nonresonant component and leaves p_b. If p_b=0, z is an additional eigenvector independent of E and completes an eigenbasis. If p_b≠0, z maps to p_b under U−b and p_b maps to zero, giving a Jordan chain of length two. No chain can be longer because E is diagonal. Replacing a basis of E_b by one containing p_b leaves exactly one such chain and all remaining vectors as eigenvectors. The characteristic and minimal polynomial formulas now follow, including the case in which b equals several listed diagonal eigenvalues.

The iterate formula follows by solving y_(n+1)=b y_n+p(a^n x) and expanding the forcing into p_μ(a^j x)=μ^j p_μ(x). Induction produces the convolution sum; multiplying it by b−μ telescopes to b^n−μ^n. Resonance makes every term of the sum equal b^(n−1), which explains the factor n. Finally a polynomial fiber change H(x,y)=(x,y+h(x)) removes p entirely exactly when c_k+(a^k−b)h_k=0 for every coefficient k. This is possible precisely when all resonant c_k vanish, equivalently p_b=0, and the displayed h supplies it. All such h differ by a polynomial satisfying h(ax)=bh(x), so resonant eigenfunctions describe the freedom in the coordinate change. This is a criterion for that specified class of coordinate changes, not a classification of arbitrary polynomial conjugacies.
worked_example_json:
{"setup":"The twelve exact replay cases include generic real eigenvalues, a=0, a=1, a=−1, affine forcing, zero forcing and the complex fourth root of unity a=i. All coefficients and all calculations are rational or Gaussian-rational. The following examples expose different structural regimes.","calculation":"For a=2, b=4 and p=x²+x³, Λ={4,8}, so W_min=span{1,x,y,x²,x³} has dimension five. The b=4 component is x² and creates a size-two Jordan chain. Taking z=y−x³/4 gives Uz=4z+x². The exact iterate is y_n=4^n y+n4^(n−1)x²+(8^n−4^n)x³/4 for n≥1. This is a nonlinear map with a finite exact linear feature evolution, and the resonant term has the predicted n factor.

For a=−1, b=1 and p=x²+2x³+3x⁴, the even powers form v_+=x²+3x⁴ and the odd power forms v_−=2x³. Dimension is five rather than the six obtained by retaining every monomial separately. The shifted coordinate z=y+x³ satisfies Uz=z+v_+, so the minimal polynomial is (t−1)²(t+1). For a=0, b=0 and p=3+2x+x²+2x⁵, the single nonlinear group is q=x²+2x⁵, dimension is four, and z=y−3 satisfies Uz=2x+q and U²z=0. This is the zero-eigenvalue Jordan case, not a reason to discard q.

For a=i and p=x²+x⁶+2x³+3x⁷+x⁴+x⁸, six nonlinear monomials collapse into the three residue groups modulo four, so dimension is six. Their eigenvalues are −1,−i,1. Choosing b=−1 creates a resonant chain; choosing b=2 does not. Conversely, a=2,b=3,p=3+2x+x²+x³ has no resonance: z=y+3/2+2x−x²−x³/5 gives the actual two-coordinate linear dynamics x′=2x,z′=3z. Nevertheless any invariant linear space required to contain the original y still needs the nonlinear readout features and has dimension five.

For contrast, the coupled invertible map G(x,y)=(y,y²−x) has inverse G^(−1)(x,y)=(x²−y,x). If Y_n=U_G^n y, then Y_0=y, Y_1=y²−x and Y_(n+1)=Y_n²−Y_(n−1).
